The task of the believing servant is only this: to become a caller (dāʿī) to the truth and convey it in the best manner, and not to take up the seat of divine office and issue final verdicts.

This law has also passed through an evolutionary process. Among the earliest peoples, Allah the Exalted made direct heavenly calamities the means of the punishment of extirpation (ʿadhāb al-istiʾṣāl). But with the evolution of human consciousness and after the finality of prophethood, this same law entered a new phase, in which the practical striving of the believers, their struggle and jihad, was made the means of enforcing punishment instead of heavenly calamities. The history from Prophet Moses to the era of the Prophet ﷺ bears witness that when the proof of the truth is complete, human hands must now become the instrument for carrying out God’s justice. This is not mere defence. It is an organised legal and divine rule for bringing falsehood to an end.

### Note: Research Methodology

The following principles have been kept in view in this study:

- **Encouraging criticism:** Readers are invited that if they find better and solid arguments, they should adopt them and inform us, so that the error can be corrected.
- **Resolve to correct:** We make a firm resolve that if we come to realise an error in our earlier research, whether after one year or after fifty years, we will retract publicly and stop the publication of our writings.
- **Qur’anic principle:** The scholarly method of this research is subject to the Qur’anic principle “those who listen to the word and follow the best of it” (39:18). Its purpose is the mere acquisition of knowledge, not any personal fame or the defence of a theory.

>> ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحۡسَنَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ وَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ

*“Who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones Allah has guided, and those are people of understanding”* (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:18 · trans. Sahih International)

## First Condition: The Truth Made Clear and the Proof Established

According to the wise Qur’an, the first and fundamental condition before the descent of divine punishment is that the truth be made so clear from Allah the Exalted that no excuse remains for man. This principle is supported by Sūrat al-Nisāʾ (4:165), where it is said:

>> رُّسُلٗا مُّبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ حُجَّةُۢ بَعۡدَ ٱلرُّسُلِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمٗا

*“[We sent] messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise”* (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:165 · trans. Sahih International)

This verse makes it clear, at the level of ʿibārat al-naṣṣ (the explicit wording of the text), that after the coming of the messengers the excuse of the people will not be accepted. In the same way, Sūrat al-Isrāʾ (17:15) states this principle more explicitly:

>> مَّنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهۡتَدِي لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡهَاۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٞ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبۡعَثَ رَسُولٗا

*“Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger”* (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:15 · trans. Sahih International)

This verse too, under ʿibārat al-naṣṣ, directly makes the sending of a messenger a necessary precondition of punishment.

The reference to Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ (28:59) is also very important in this connection. Allah says:

>> وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ مُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡعَثَ فِيٓ أُمِّهَا رَسُولٗا يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَاۚ وَمَا كُنَّا مُهۡلِكِي ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ إِلَّا وَأَهۡلُهَا ظَٰلِمُونَ

*“And never would your Lord have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their mother a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers”* (Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:59 · trans. Sahih International)

Its fundamental level is ʿibārat al-naṣṣ, which explicitly makes the prior presence of a messenger and the recitation of the verses necessary before destruction. Under this same principle it is said in Sūrat al-Anʿām (6:131):

>> ذَٰلِكَ أَن لَّمۡ يَكُن رَّبُّكَ مُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ بِظُلۡمٖ وَأَهۡلُهَا غَٰفِلُونَ

*“That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities for wrongdoing while their people were unaware”* (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:131 · trans. Sahih International)

Its fundamental level is dalālat al-naṣṣ (the implication of the text), from which it is deduced that Allah the Exalted does not destroy any people until they have been fully informed of the facts.

In Sūrat al-Naḥl (16:36) this divine sunnah is repeated:

>> وَلَقَدۡ بَعَثۡنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٖ رَّسُولًا أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱجۡتَنِبُواْ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتَۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ حَقَّتۡ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُۚ فَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ

*“And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut." And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So proceed through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers”* (Sūrat al-Naḥl 16:36 · trans. Sahih International)

The fundamental level of this verse too is ʿibārat al-naṣṣ, which establishes that conveying the call to every community is Allah’s eternal sunnah. The collective result of all these verses is this: Allah never passes a decisive judgement of seizure on any people until the truth has been made fully clear through a messenger.

**Exception:** In this first stage, those people are exempt from destruction who are “ghāfil” (heedless), that is, those to whom the call of the truth and the message of the messenger has not reached. Allah’s justice demands that no one be punished before clear exposition and awareness of the truth. This exception exists because the enforcement of punishment is possible only after the completion of proof, and this law does not seize those who remain uninformed of the message of truth. From this explicit rule of the noble Qur’an it becomes clear that Allah’s attribute of justice makes it necessary that people be fully informed of the facts before a decisive judgement. Therefore those who have, as yet, no knowledge of the call to the truth are kept safe, by the general mercy of Allah, from the punishment of extirpation.

## Second Condition: Wrongdoing, Corruption and Deviation from Reform

The first stage made it clear that, according to the Qur’an, no decisive punishment comes before the proof is established. The question now is: after the proof is established, what is the state that makes a people deserving of punishment? The Qur’an tells us again and again that the problem of the punished peoples was not merely “error”. It was deviation: wrongdoing (ẓulm), corruption (fasād), arrogance, rebellion and the refusal of reform. In this connection it is said in Sūrat Hūd (11:102):

>> وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَخۡذُ رَبِّكَ إِذَآ أَخَذَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ وَهِيَ ظَٰلِمَةٌۚ إِنَّ أَخۡذَهُۥٓ أَلِيمٞ شَدِيدٌ

*“And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:102 · trans. Sahih International)

The text makes it clear that when Allah seizes the towns, they are “wrongdoing” (ẓālimah). In the same way, in Sūrat Hūd (11:117):

>> وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ بِظُلۡمٖ وَأَهۡلُهَا مُصۡلِحُونَ

*“And your Lord would not have destroyed the cities unjustly while their people were reformers”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:117 · trans. Sahih International)

Through this verse the principle is stated that as long as the people of a town are reformers (muṣliḥūn), destruction does not come. From this it is known, by dalālat al-naṣṣ, that a state of corruption is a condition for destruction.

Further, it is said in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ (17:16):

>> وَإِذَآ أَرَدۡنَآ أَن نُّهۡلِكَ قَرۡيَةً أَمَرۡنَا مُتۡرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُواْ فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيۡهَا ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فَدَمَّرۡنَٰهَا تَدۡمِيرٗا

*“And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with [complete] destruction”* (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:16 · trans. Sahih International)

Here fisq (transgression) is given as the cause of the decision of destruction. In Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ (28:58) it is said:

>> وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَرۡيَةِۭ بَطِرَتۡ مَعِيشَتَهَاۖ فَتِلۡكَ مَسَٰكِنُهُمۡ لَمۡ تُسۡكَن مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗاۖ وَكُنَّا نَحۡنُ ٱلۡوَٰرِثِينَ

*“And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who were the inheritors”* (Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:58 · trans. Sahih International)

Here “baṭirat maʿīshatahā” (“they exulted in their livelihood”) makes it a backdrop of destruction that they became arrogant and rebellious through the luxury of their living. In the case of Pharaoh it is made clear in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf (7:103):

>> ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَاۖ فَٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ

*“Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, but they were unjust toward them. So see how was the end of the corrupters”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:103 · trans. Sahih International)

Finally, the explicit statement in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt (29:31):

>> وَلَمَّا جَآءَتۡ رُسُلُنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلۡبُشۡرَىٰ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا مُهۡلِكُوٓاْ أَهۡلِ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِۖ إِنَّ أَهۡلَهَا كَانُواْ ظَٰلِمِينَ

*“And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of that Lot's city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers”* (Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:31 · trans. Sahih International)

makes the gravity of this stage fully clear.

**Exception:** It is necessary to understand that the mere existence of wrongdoing and corruption (the second condition) is not by itself sufficient for the enforcement of punishment. The law of divine justice requires that the punishment of extirpation not descend until all the remaining stages are complete: the full clarity of the truth (the first condition), the continuity of warnings (the third condition), and the decisive completion of the proof (the fourth condition). Therefore, at this stage too, those people are exempt from punishment who live in an apparent environment of corruption. The enforcement of divine punishment is possible only when crime reaches its final limit and all the requirements of the proof are fulfilled.

## Third Condition: Warnings, Trials and the Lesser Punishment

From the manner described by the Qur’an it is known that Allah the Exalted does not seize most peoples in the final grip immediately. He first gives them the opportunity to turn back, through admonition, trial, hardship and smaller seizures. In Sūrat al-Sajdah (32:21) this is explicit:

>> وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ

*“And we will surely let them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment that perhaps they will repent”* (Sūrat al-Sajdah 32:21 · trans. Sahih International)

Here the purpose of al-ʿadhāb al-adnā (the lesser punishment) is stated as “laʿallahum yarjiʿūn” (“perhaps they will return”). In the same way it is said in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf (7:94):

>> وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِي قَرۡيَةٖ مِّن نَّبِيٍّ إِلَّآ أَخَذۡنَآ أَهۡلَهَا بِٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَضَّرَّعُونَ

*“And We sent to no city a prophet [who was denied] except that We seized its people with poverty and hardship that they might humble themselves [to Allah]”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:94 · trans. Sahih International)

In Sūrat al-Anʿām (6:42) this method is stated as a general sunnah:

>> وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمَمٖ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُم بِٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ

*“And We have already sent [messengers] to nations before you, [O Muhammad]; then We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they might humble themselves [to Us]”* (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:42 · trans. Sahih International)

Even after the seizure has come, hearts may remain hard, as it is said in Sūrat al-Anʿām (6:43):

>> فَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ جَآءَهُم بَأۡسُنَا تَضَرَّعُواْ وَلَٰكِن قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ

*“Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them that which they were doing”* (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:43 · trans. Sahih International)

This decision, to harden the heart instead of humbling oneself, is a sign of deviation. The succession of warnings is mentioned in Sūrat al-Zukhruf (43:48):

>> وَمَا نُرِيهِم مِّنۡ ءَايَةٍ إِلَّا هِيَ أَكۡبَرُ مِنۡ أُخۡتِهَاۖ وَأَخَذۡنَٰهُم بِٱلۡعَذَابِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ

*“And We showed them not a sign except that it was greater than its sister, and We seized them with affliction that perhaps they might return [to faith]”* (Sūrat al-Zukhruf 43:48 · trans. Sahih International)

About Pharaoh, Sūrat al-Aʿrāf (7:130) tells us:

>> وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ وَنَقۡصٖ مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَذَّكَّرُونَ

*“And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a deficiency in fruits that perhaps they would be reminded”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:130 · trans. Sahih International)

All these verses make it clear that the small warnings that come before the great seizure are part of itmām al-ḥujjah.

**Exception:** Warnings and trials (the third condition) do not by themselves become the prelude to punishment until all four conditions have reached completion. Allah’s law of punishment does not move until the truth is fully clear, wrongdoing and corruption reach their limit, and all the requirements of the proof are fulfilled. Therefore, at this stage too, those people are exempt for whom the trial has come, but from whose side the final and decisive denial, which becomes the real trigger for the descent of divine punishment, has not yet appeared.

## Fourth Condition: “Lā Yuʾminūn” — The Final State of Denial

In the earlier stages, the truth was made clear, the proof was established, and wrongdoing, corruption and warnings took place. After these, the Qur’an describes a state in which no possibility remains that the people will accept faith, because of their continuous denial and obstinacy. It is said in Sūrat Yūnus (10:96–97):

>> إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ ۝٩٦ وَلَوۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ كُلُّ ءَايَةٍ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ ۝٩٧

*“Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment”* (Sūrat Yūnus 10:96–97 · trans. Sahih International)

In the same way it is said in Sūrat Yā-Sīn (36:7):

>> لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ

*“Already the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe”* (Sūrat Yā-Sīn 36:7 · trans. Sahih International)

and in verse 10:

>> وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ

*“And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe”* (Sūrat Yā-Sīn 36:10 · trans. Sahih International)

Through these verses the decisive denial is made clear.

In Sūrat al-Baqarah (2:6–7) this psychological state of the deniers is described in this way:

>> إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ ۝٦ خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَعَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِمۡۖ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ غِشَٰوَةٞۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٞ ۝٧

*“Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment”* (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:6–7 · trans. Sahih International)

In Sūrat al-Aʿrāf (7:101) the sealing of hearts is mentioned:

>> تِلۡكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآئِهَاۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَطۡبَعُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ

*“Those cities - We relate to you, [O Muhammad], some of their news. And certainly did their messengers come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of the disbelievers”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:101 · trans. Sahih International)

while in verse 146 of the same sūrah arrogance is given as the cause of being deprived of the signs:

>> سَأَصۡرِفُ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ كُلَّ ءَايَةٖ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِهَا وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرُّشۡدِ لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلٗا وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلۡغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلٗاۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡهَا غَٰفِلِينَ

*“I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right; and if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the way of consciousness, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way. That is because they have denied Our signs and they were heedless of them”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:146 · trans. Sahih International)

This final stage reveals the last human state before the decision of punishment: after continuous denial, the possibility of faith has come to an end.

**Exception:** According to the Qur’anic law of punishment, the seizure takes effect only when all four conditions have come together: the clear exposition of the truth, corruption, warnings, and denial. Even at this fourth and final stage there are exceptions of two kinds. First, there are those individuals who are, as yet, in a state of denial or of sincere seeking of the truth. The decisive judgement of itmām al-ḥujjah is not a human decision but a divine prerogative, so these remain within the circle of Allah’s general mercy. Second, there are those groups who, after itmām al-ḥujjah, make a treaty of peace (muʿāhadah) with the Muslims, or are overpowered and accept submission (ṣāghirūn), as mentioned in Sūrat al-Tawbah (9:29). They are exempt from the punishment of extirpation (complete ending). Therefore the enforcement of divine punishment is only for those obstinate ones who, even after the truth had become clear, chose rebellion and corruption as their settled path.

## Application of the Stages of Itmām al-Ḥujjah to Earlier Peoples

After completing the theoretical discussions, we now turn to the practical application of the law of itmām al-ḥujjah. The noble Qur’an has preserved this law, with an imperishable wisdom, through the stories of the prophets. These stories are not mere historical events. They are proofs of that divine rule by which the truth was made manifest stage by stage, the proof was completed from every side, and finally the justice of Allah appeared in its full majesty.

In this practical study we will examine the history of each people: through which stages the call to the truth passed, and at which point the people’s denial moved beyond mere disagreement and took the form of continuous denial and corruption. This analysis will make clear that the punishment of extirpation never came suddenly or without cause. Before it, all the doors of mercy were opened, and the truth was made so bright that no legitimate excuse remained for denial.

### 1. The People of Noah: The First Practical Example of the Law of Itmām al-Ḥujjah

The first practical example of these attributes of itmām al-ḥujjah and of the punishment of extirpation in human history is seen in the people of Noah (peace be upon him). In terms of time, this people was among the earliest peoples after Adam (peace be upon him). It was the first corrupt generation in human history, one that had sunk into such depths of idol-worship that it flatly refused to abandon its false gods. The light of guidance had grown dim among them. Their obstinacy was such that they taught this same lesson to the generations that came after them:

>> وَقَالُواْ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدّٗا وَلَا سُوَاعٗا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسۡرٗا

*“And said, 'Never leave your gods and never leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr”* (Sūrat Nūḥ 71:23 · trans. Sahih International)

To cleanse the earth of corruption and to call them back to pure tawḥīd, the justice of Allah sent Noah (peace be upon him) as His messenger, that is, as the final proof upon his own people:

>> إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ أَنۡ أَنذِرۡ قَوۡمَكَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٞ

*“Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment”* (Sūrat Nūḥ 71:1 · trans. Sahih International)

When Noah (peace be upon him) began his call, it was not a mere series of advice. It was the enforcement of the conclusive proof (ḥujjah bālighah) from Allah. He laboured for a long period: day and night, secretly and openly. In every way he made the truth so plain that no excuse of ignorance remained for those who denied it (71:5–9, 11:27). The Qur’an expressed it in these words:

>> وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرٞ مُّبِينٌ

*“And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:25 · trans. Sahih International)

Here the word “mubīn” (clear) is a decisive proof that Noah’s (peace be upon him) call left no room for any doubt or ambiguity. The enemy people had no logical argument with which to refute the truth (11:27, 23:24), except that they persisted in pride and arrogance (71:7).

The truth had become so plain and bright that no kind of ambiguity remained in it. Despite this, the people’s reaction did not stop at denial. It rose to severity. But the eternal rule of divine justice is that a decision of punishment is not made on the basis of mere initial denial and corruption. Even to a rebellious people, the opportunity to return (repentance) and to reform is given widely and for a long time, so that the proof may be completed upon them from every side. Noah (peace be upon him) not only informed them of the signs of punishment. In deep compassion he also called them to return, becoming a means of Allah’s grace and wide mercy. The Qur’an describes this great call to return and the wide scope of Allah’s mercy in these words:

>> فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارٗا ۝١٠ يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّدۡرَارٗا ۝١١ وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلٖ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٖ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡهَٰرٗا ۝١٢

*“And said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers And give you increase in wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers”* (Sūrat Nūḥ 71:10–12 · trans. Sahih International)

These verses are a bright proof that the people were given full opportunity for repentance and reform. But in this long period the people’s obstinacy and the trial of Noah (peace be upon him) continued side by side. The Qur’an describes it in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt (29:14) in a very subtle, eloquent and meaningful style:

>> وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامٗا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ

*“And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers”* (Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:14 · trans. Sahih International)

Here the Qur’anic choice of words has a deep eloquence built into it. In the Arabic language and the Qur’anic style, the word “sanah” (year) is used for years of hardship, difficulty and trial, while the word “ʿām” (year) is used for years of ease, comfort and prosperity. In this way the verse tells us that most of the period of Noah’s (peace be upon him) call was filled with the severe opposition of the people, with harm and rebellion (sanah), while only a small part (ʿām) was one of ordinary ease and comfort. It is as if, despite such a long respite, continual advice and the compassion of Allah’s mercy in the call, the people’s reaction became harsher still. Here the Qur’an makes clear a fixed and eternal law of divine justice: Allah does not send down punishment directly at once. He first afflicts peoples with hardship and distress, so that they may adopt humility and return (7:94–95).

The people of Noah (peace be upon him) were also shaken by these warning punishments, but even these warning punishments could not break their arrogance. They stayed fixed in their obstinacy: they thrust their fingers into their ears and covered their faces with their garments (71:7). Their corruption had reached such a social level that they rejected the truth merely because the followers of Noah (peace be upon him) belonged to the lowly and humble classes of society (11:27, 26:111). When argument and warning both proved ineffective, their obstinacy turned into open terror. They gave the Messenger, the last of the proofs, a threat of killing:

>> قَالُواْ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ يَٰنُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَرۡجُومِينَ

*“They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be of those who are stoned”* (Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:116 · trans. Sahih International)

But the justice of Allah’s messenger is neither overawed by material power nor does it retreat before threats of murder. In answer to this open terror, instead of being cowed or hiding, Noah (peace be upon him) made such a majestic and conquering announcement that it exposed the arrogance of the people and the helplessness of their false gods. The Qur’an preserves this stage of the completion of proof in these words, in Sūrat Yūnus:

>> ۞وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذۡ قَالَ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيۡكُم مَّقَامِي وَتَذۡكِيرِي بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُ فَأَجۡمِعُوٓاْ أَمۡرَكُمۡ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنۡ أَمۡرُكُمۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غُمَّةٗ ثُمَّ ٱقۡضُوٓاْ إِلَيَّ وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ

*“And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, "O my people, if my residence and my reminding of the signs of Allah has become burdensome upon you - then I have relied upon Allah. So resolve upon your plan and [call upon] your associates. Then let not your plan be obscure to you. Then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite”* (Sūrat Yūnus 10:71 · trans. Sahih International)

Along with this, he also presented the final argument for the selflessness of his call:

>> فَإِن تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ فَمَا سَأَلۡتُكُم مِّنۡ أَجۡرٍۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَأُمِرۡتُ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ

*“And if you turn away [from my advice] then no payment have I asked of you. My reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be of the Muslims”* (Sūrat Yūnus 10:72 · trans. Sahih International)

For a single, lone prophet to challenge an entire armed and hostile people so openly was the greatest proof of the truthfulness of the truth. By this challenge the proof upon them was completed to its final degree. Despite this, when the people did not turn away from their obstinacy, it was certain proof that the possibility of return had ended for them forever.

During the call of Noah (peace be upon him), the constant reaction of the people’s rebellion and insolence was that they mocked the truth and, in mockery, repeatedly demanded the punishment, saying:

>> قَالُواْ يَٰنُوحُ قَدۡ جَٰدَلۡتَنَا فَأَكۡثَرۡتَ جِدَٰلَنَا فَأۡتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ

*“They said, "O Noah, you have disputed us and been frequent in dispute of us. So bring us what you threaten us, if you should be of the truthful”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:32 · trans. Sahih International)

In reply to this arrogant demand, the messenger of divine justice knew his limits and the authority of Allah the Exalted very well. So Noah (peace be upon him) answered with great dignity and decisiveness:

>> قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَأۡتِيكُم بِهِ ٱللَّهُ إِن شَآءَ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُعۡجِزِينَ

*“He said, "Allah will only bring it to you if He wills, and you will not cause [Him] failure”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:33 · trans. Sahih International)

When denial, corruption and obstinacy reached their end and the possibility of return was over, the decisive judgement descended from the heavens, and Allah the Exalted set His final seal on this matter:

>> وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤۡمِنَ مِن قَوۡمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدۡ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبۡتَئِسۡ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ

*“And it was revealed to Noah that, "No one will believe from your people except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:36 · trans. Sahih International)

This verse was not merely a report. It was the decisive judgement of divine justice, which made it clear that the proof had reached its end and that no room for faith remained for this people.

When the revelation of “lā yuʾminūn” revealed this truth fully, that none of this corrupt generation would bring faith, then Noah (peace be upon him), on the basis of divine justice, made that great final prayer that is preserved in Sūrat Nūḥ:

>> وَقَالَ نُوحٞ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرۡ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا ۝٢٦ إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرۡهُمۡ يُضِلُّواْ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓاْ إِلَّا فَاجِرٗا كَفَّارٗا ۝٢٧

*“And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and not beget except [every] wicked one and [confirmed] disbeliever”* (Sūrat Nūḥ 71:26–27 · trans. Sahih International)

This prayer was not an expression of personal revenge or an emotional reaction. It was the result of the certain knowledge obtained through the revelation of Allah the Exalted, that granting this people further respite would only become a cause for spreading corruption more widely against the truth.

In compliance with the command of Allah, when Noah (peace be upon him) began to build the ship, the world of ignorance and arrogance of the people showed itself. Whenever their chiefs passed by him, they would mock and ridicule this work. But Noah (peace be upon him), unmoved by this mockery, replied with complete certainty in Allah’s promise:

>> وَيَصۡنَعُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَأٞ مِّن قَوۡمِهِۦ سَخِرُواْ مِنۡهُۚ قَالَ إِن تَسۡخَرُواْ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسۡخَرُ مِنكُمۡ كَمَا تَسۡخَرُونَ ۝٣٨ فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ مَن يَأۡتِيهِ عَذَابٞ يُخۡزِيهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيۡهِ عَذَابٞ مُّقِيمٌ ۝٣٩

*“And he constructed the ship, and whenever an assembly of the eminent of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, "If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule And you are going to know who will get a punishment that will disgrace him [on earth] and upon whom will descend an enduring punishment [in the Hereafter]”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:38–39 · trans. Sahih International)

This dignified reply, spoken with full certainty, said that the mockery of falsehood lasts only a few days, while the punishment of Allah the Exalted that is coming is eternal. Soon the people would see the reality: upon whom the humiliating punishment descends, and for whom the lasting punishment is decreed.

We now reach the last and most majestic stage of this series. The punishment of extirpation, in this world and in the barzakh (the interval between death and resurrection), arrives. When the time fixed by divine justice came and the last moment of respite ended, the first sign of the punishment appeared:

>> حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلۡنَا ٱحۡمِلۡ فِيهَا مِن كُلّٖ زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ وَأَهۡلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ وَمَنۡ ءَامَنَۚ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٞ

*“[So it was], until when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, "Load upon the ship of each [creature] two mates and your family, except those about whom the word has preceded, and [include] whoever has believed." But none had believed with him, except a few”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:40 · trans. Sahih International)

This was the announcement that the time to purify the earth of the corrupt had begun. Under divine command, Noah (peace be upon him) took on the ship two pairs of everything necessary, his family (except those against whom the word had already been decreed), and the few believers who had brought faith (11:40).

After this the punishment of extirpation descended in its full majesty. The earth and the sky, in obedience to Allah’s command, carried out the punishment, and a terrifying scene was established. The Qur’an describes this majesty in these words:

>> فَفَتَحۡنَآ أَبۡوَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَآءٖ مُّنۡهَمِرٖ ۝١١ وَفَجَّرۡنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ عُيُونٗا فَٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرٖ قَدۡ قُدِرَ ۝١٢

*“Then We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down And caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already predestined”* (Sūrat al-Qamar 54:11–12 · trans. Sahih International)

In this grave stage, the great scene of the impartial justice (Impartial Justice) of divine justice came before us, which made it clear that in the divine law mere blood relations have no standing. Noah’s (peace be upon him) own son was also among the deniers. When the water rose toward the mountains, the father, in compassion, called out once more:

>> وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجٖ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلٖ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ

*“And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son who was apart [from them], "O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:42 · trans. Sahih International)

But the son’s arrogance and his reliance on material means were still intact, and he replied:

>> قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٖ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ

*“[But] he said, "I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water." [Noah] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He gives mercy." And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:43 · trans. Sahih International)

At that very moment a great wave came, and he became one of the drowned. When Noah (peace be upon him) cried out to Allah for the deliverance of his son (11:45), the decisive judgement was announced from the justice of Allah:

>> قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيۡسَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيۡرُ صَٰلِحٖۖ فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۖ إِنِّيٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ

*“He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:46 · trans. Sahih International)

This decision established the example, until the Day of Judgement, that deliverance does not depend on ties of blood. It depends on faith and deeds. To restore the balance of the earth, the whole corrupt people were drowned in this great flood. But the law of recompense was not limited to the water of this world. Immediately after their drowning, the punishment of the fire of the barzakh was imposed on them. The Qur’an describes this immediate punishment in a majestic manner:

>> مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمۡ أُغۡرِقُواْ فَأُدۡخِلُواْ نَارٗا فَلَمۡ يَجِدُواْ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارٗا

*“Because of their sins they were drowned and put into the Fire, and they found not for themselves besides Allah [any] helpers”* (Sūrat Nūḥ 71:25 · trans. Sahih International)

From this verse it is clear that the punishment of extirpation was not limited to this world. Immediately after the drowning, the punishment of the barzakh began for them, and the double punishment of this world and the barzakh, which would never end, would be theirs. Only Noah (peace be upon him) and those who believed in him were able to find deliverance from this double punishment. After the roots of the corrupt people were cut off, divine justice announced the decision:

>> وَقِيلَ يَـٰٓأَرۡضُ ٱبۡلَعِي مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقۡلِعِي وَغِيضَ ٱلۡمَآءُ وَقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ وَٱسۡتَوَتۡ عَلَى ٱلۡجُودِيِّۖ وَقِيلَ بُعۡدٗا لِّلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ

*“And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]." And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mountain of] Judiyy. And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:44 · trans. Sahih International)

The earth was purified, and Allah advanced the new line of humanity through those survivors who were devoted to the truth:

>> وَجَعَلۡنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥ هُمُ ٱلۡبَاقِينَ

*“And We made his descendants those remaining [on the earth]”* (Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt 37:77 · trans. Sahih International)

so that the coming generations might take a lesson from this great decision of divine justice and from this prelude to the struggle between truth and falsehood.

### 2. The People of ʿĀd (Sayyidunā Hūd): The Arrogance of Power and the Punishment of the Ṣarṣar Wind

After the punishment of extirpation upon the people of Noah (peace be upon him), the earth was cleansed of shirk and corruption, and divine justice advanced a new line of guidance through the believers. But as centuries passed, the human race once again turned away from the light of tawḥīd and fell into shirk, pride and corruption. This was the second practical stage of the law of itmām al-ḥujjah: the trial of the people of ʿĀd. This people was the most prominent of its age in material progress, in physical strength, in grandeur, and in its architectural abilities. Tall and lofty buildings were the clear sign of their rise. The Qur’an describes their extraordinary rise and their corruption in these words:

>> إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلۡعِمَادِ ۝٧ ٱلَّتِي لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ ۝٨

*“[With] Iram - who had lofty pillars The likes of whom had never been created in the land”* (Sūrat al-Fajr 89:7–8 · trans. Sahih International)

Then they carried corruption in the land to its extreme. But this same material power and progress, when it took the form of arrogance, became a means of corruption on earth. So the Qur’an says:

>> فَأَكۡثَرُواْ فِيهَا ٱلۡفَسَادَ

*“And increased therein the corruption”* (Sūrat al-Fajr 89:12 · trans. Sahih International)

When the material power of the people of ʿĀd became a means of shirk, arrogance and corruption, the justice of Allah, to bring them back to the truth, sent among them their own brother Hūd (peace be upon him) as a messenger and as the final proof. Hūd (peace be upon him) began his call on exactly the same fundamental principle with which every messenger begins, namely, the call to tawḥīd. The Qur’an describes this beginning in these words:

>> ۞وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمۡ هُودٗاۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥٓۚ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

*“And to the 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:65 · trans. Sahih International)

While presenting the call to tawḥīd, and in order to establish the proof upon this corrupt people, Hūd (peace be upon him) reminded them of the position, the power and the inheritance of the earth that Allah had granted them after the people of Noah, so that they might awaken from this material intoxication:

>> أَوَعَجِبۡتُمۡ أَن جَآءَكُمۡ ذِكۡرٞ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٖ مِّنكُمۡ لِيُنذِرَكُمۡۚ وَٱذۡكُرُوٓاْ إِذۡ جَعَلَكُمۡ خُلَفَآءَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ قَوۡمِ نُوحٖ وَزَادَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡخَلۡقِ بَصۜۡطَةٗۖ فَٱذۡكُرُوٓاْ ءَالَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ

*“Then do you wonder that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you, that he may warn you? And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature extensively. So remember the favors of Allah that you might succeed”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:69 · trans. Sahih International)

From this verse it is clear that Hūd (peace be upon him) did not only stop his people from shirk. He also made them remember this feeling about their history: that the One who gave them this position and the power granted by Allah, and the responsibility that comes with it, has the right to true obedience. In this way the call to tawḥīd did not remain limited to the correction of belief. It became the beginning of the practical enforcement of the law of itmām al-ḥujjah.

This call was not limited to the correction of belief. The demand of divine justice was that the chain of corruption and oppression they had established on the earth be stopped. In reality this corruption was not merely the result of ignorance. Material power, wealth and the pride of their progress had taken them far from the truth. The most prominent expression of this arrogance was seen in their style of construction. They were so blinded by pride that on every high place they would set up purposeless landmarks. The Qur’an exposes this attitude:

>> أَتَبۡنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ ءَايَةٗ تَعۡبَثُونَ ۝١٢٨ وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَخۡلُدُونَ ۝١٢٩ وَإِذَا بَطَشۡتُم بَطَشۡتُمۡ جَبَّارِينَ ۝١٣٠

*“Do you construct on every elevation a sign, amusing yourselves And take for yourselves palaces and fortresses that you might abide eternally And when you strike, you strike as tyrants”* (Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:128–130 · trans. Sahih International)

This same arrogance made them dare to rely on their physical strength in the face of the divine law, so much so that with extreme insolence they announced:

>> فَأَمَّا عَادٞ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَقَالُواْ مَنۡ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةًۖ أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُمۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةٗۖ وَكَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يَجۡحَدُونَ

*“As for 'Aad, they were arrogant upon the earth without right and said, "Who is greater than us in strength?" Did they not consider that Allah who created them was greater than them in strength? But they were rejecting Our signs”* (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:15 · trans. Sahih International)

This continuous call of Hūd (peace be upon him) was in reality the enforcement of the conclusive proof (ḥujjah bālighah) from the divine law. He explained tawḥīd, Allah’s blessings and the end of the people of ʿĀd in such a clear and luminous manner that the truth became manifest to them from every aspect, and for those who denied it no room for misunderstanding or ignorance was left. To bring this conclusive proof to its final degree, Hūd (peace be upon him) also presented clear evidence of his selflessness and sincerity. He said:

>> يَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ

*“O my people, I do not ask you for it any reward. My reward is only from the one who created me. Then will you not reason”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:51 · trans. Sahih International)

By this selfless call he completed the proof upon the people of ʿĀd. When a messenger neither seeks any worldly benefit for his call nor demands any reward from anyone, the truthfulness and sincerity of his call themselves become a bright proof that he is on the truth.

Despite this, the people, instead of accepting the truth, persisted in their arrogance. Instead of meeting the truth with argument, they began to target the person of the messenger. The Qur’an has preserved this insolence in these words:

>> قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰكَ فِي سَفَاهَةٖ وَإِنَّا لَنَظُنُّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ

*“Said the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people, "Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are of the liars”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:66 · trans. Sahih International)

This accusation was not based on any rational or textual argument. It was an arrogant attempt, made by those unable to confront the truth, to make the person of the messenger their target. Hūd (peace be upon him), instead of anger or revenge, answered this with great dignity and forbearance:

>> قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ لَيۡسَ بِي سَفَاهَةٞ وَلَٰكِنِّي رَسُولٞ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ ۝٦٧ أُبَلِّغُكُمۡ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّي وَأَنَا۠ لَكُمۡ نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ ۝٦٨

*“[Hud] said, "O my people, there is not foolishness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am to you a trustworthy adviser”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:67–68 · trans. Sahih International)

It is an eternal rule of the divine law that punishment is not sent down merely on the basis of initial denial. According to the principle of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf (7:94), Allah the Exalted, before the final punishment, afflicted the people of ʿĀd with the “ʿadhāb adnā” (lesser punishment) in order to awaken them. Their unparalleled prosperity, material power and pride in physical strength were broken by Allah the Exalted, by trying them with drought and famine, so that they might adopt humility.

During this trial and “lesser punishment” too, Hūd (peace be upon him), with great compassion, invited them again and again to repentance, through the grace and wide mercy of Allah the Exalted. The Qur’an describes this call to return in these words:

>> وَيَٰقَوۡمِ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّدۡرَارٗا وَيَزِدۡكُمۡ قُوَّةً إِلَىٰ قُوَّتِكُمۡ وَلَا تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ مُجۡرِمِينَ

*“And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength [added] to your strength. And do not turn away, [being] criminals”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:52 · trans. Sahih International)

This verse is decisive proof that divine justice had given them a full opportunity of return, forgiveness, and the restoration of His blessings.

But despite this warning and call to return, their arrogance and rebellion increased still more. They not only rejected the conclusive proof. With blind attachment to their false gods, they denied it outright:

>> قَالُواْ يَٰهُودُ مَا جِئۡتَنَا بِبَيِّنَةٖ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِتَارِكِيٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوۡلِكَ وَمَا نَحۡنُ لَكَ بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ

*“They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us clear evidence, and we are not ones to leave our gods on your say-so. Nor are we believers in you”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:53 · trans. Sahih International)

This was not only the denial of one messenger. In reality it was a gradual denial of the fundamental principles of divine revelation. So they said that if Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels, and therefore they denied the message with which they had been sent (41:14). Here their obstinacy reached such a point that they announced: “It is the same to us whether you advise us or do not advise us” (26:136).

The result of this continuous denial and obstinacy was that corruption was not limited to belief. The whole system of society came into its grip. The Qur’an exposes this severe social corruption in these words:

>> وَتِلۡكَ عَادٞۖ جَحَدُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَعَصَوۡاْ رُسُلَهُۥ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَمۡرَ كُلِّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٖ

*“And that was 'Aad, who rejected the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every obstinate tyrant”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:59 · trans. Sahih International)

That is, the leadership of society had fallen into the hands of arrogant and rebellious chiefs who were themselves deniers of the truth and had become a means of preventing others from it (11:59, 41:15).

Along with this obstinacy, when their material power and the pride in their false gods reached its peak, they levelled a terrible and insulting accusation against the messenger of divine justice. They claimed that, because of his denial of their gods, some of their gods had afflicted him with evil (11:54). They said: “Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful” (46:22, 7:70). When they had no logical answer left, they repeated the corrupt history of the people of Noah (peace be upon him) exactly, and with a last insolence they demanded the punishment of extirpation directly (7:70).

In answer to this arrogant demand, the messenger of divine justice knew very well his own limits and the powers of Allah the Exalted. So Hūd (peace be upon him) answered with great dignity and decisiveness:

>> قَالَ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡعِلۡمُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأُبَلِّغُكُم مَّآ أُرۡسِلۡتُ بِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمٗا تَجۡهَلُونَ

*“He said, "Knowledge [of its time] is only with Allah, and I convey to you that with which I was sent; but I see you [to be] a people behaving ignorantly”* (Sūrat al-Aḥqāf 46:23 · trans. Sahih International)

(See also 7:68.)

When they threatened the messenger of divine justice with the harm of their lifeless false gods, Hūd (peace be upon him) answered this open misguidance, not by being overawed, but by making that majestic and decisive announcement of the completion of proof, with which he exposed for the last time the helplessness of all their material power and false gods. Hūd (peace be upon him), without any fear, declared his disassociation from their false gods:

>> إِن نَّقُولُ إِلَّا ٱعۡتَرَىٰكَ بَعۡضُ ءَالِهَتِنَا بِسُوٓءٖۗ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أُشۡهِدُ ٱللَّهَ وَٱشۡهَدُوٓاْ أَنِّي بَرِيٓءٞ مِّمَّا تُشۡرِكُونَ ۝٥٤ مِن دُونِهِۦۖ فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعٗا ثُمَّ لَا تُنظِرُونِ ۝٥٥

*“We only say that some of our gods have possessed you with evil." He said, "Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and witness [yourselves] that I am free from whatever you associate with Allah Other than Him. So plot against me all together; then do not give me respite”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:54–55 · trans. Sahih International)

And along with it, he made that great declaration of his complete trust:

>> إِنِّي تَوَكَّلۡتُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمۚ مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذُۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٖ

*“Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a path [that is] straight”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:56 · trans. Sahih International)

For a single prophet to challenge in this open manner a people intoxicated with physical power, pride and arrogance was the greatest proof of the truthfulness of the message. By this open challenge he completed the proof upon them to its final degree.

The denial of the people of ʿĀd was not limited to a difference of beliefs. This material arrogance had now turned into open corruption and had descended into the veins of society. Their immense material progress and physical power had turned society into a system in which power itself had become the criterion of truth. Even though the proof of divine justice was fully clear, the majority of the people, instead of using their reason, began to follow arrogant and oppressive chiefs blindly, and tried to suppress the truth by the force of power. Corruption and obstinacy had reached their limit, and every door of return was closed. So the proof had reached its last stage, and divine justice announced its decisive judgement, which made it clear that the proof had reached its last stage and the time of respite was entirely over. Hūd (peace be upon him) said, in a decisive and majestic manner:

>> قَالَ قَدۡ وَقَعَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ رِجۡسٞ وَغَضَبٌۖ أَتُجَٰدِلُونَنِي فِيٓ أَسۡمَآءٖ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلۡطَٰنٖۚ فَٱنتَظِرُوٓاْ إِنِّي مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُنتَظِرِينَ

*“[Hud] said, "Already have defilement and anger fallen upon you from your Lord. Do you dispute with me concerning [mere] names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has not sent down any authority? Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:71 · trans. Sahih International)

This announcement of waiting was in reality the formal declaration of the completion of the proof and of the end of the respite. It meant that the proof was complete, the doors of repentance were closed, and now the decision of the heavens was about to descend upon the earth.

When the time fixed by divine justice arrived, the punishment began in the very form they had been seeking, because they had been afflicted with drought for a long period. A deep cloud appeared on the horizon of the sky. Heedless of their end, and drowned in the pride of material power, the people of ʿĀd were glad when they saw this cloud. The Qur’an describes their heedlessness and the immediate justice of Allah that followed it:

>> فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡهُ عَارِضٗا مُّسۡتَقۡبِلَ أَوۡدِيَتِهِمۡ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا عَارِضٞ مُّمۡطِرُنَاۚ بَلۡ هُوَ مَا ٱسۡتَعۡجَلۡتُم بِهِۦۖ رِيحٞ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٞ

*“And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain!" Rather, it is that for which you were impatient: a wind, within it a painful punishment”* (Sūrat al-Aḥqāf 46:24 · trans. Sahih International)

This was not an ordinary storm. It was the decisive answer of divine justice. It was a “rīḥ ṣarṣar” (a roaring wind). This punishment was in reality the decisive answer of divine justice to their extreme “corruption”, which they had spread on the earth in the intoxication of their physical power. In the pride of their power, they would lay violent hands on others, as Hūd (peace be upon him) exposed in these words:

>> وَإِذَا بَطَشۡتُم بَطَشۡتُمۡ جَبَّارِينَ

*“And when you strike, you strike as tyrants”* (Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:130 · trans. Sahih International)

The punishment of divine justice came down as a result of this same rebellion and social corruption. The Qur’an, in a most majestic style, called it “sawṭ ʿadhāb” (the whip of punishment):

>> ٱلَّذِينَ طَغَوۡاْ فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ ۝١١ فَأَكۡثَرُواْ فِيهَا ٱلۡفَسَادَ ۝١٢ فَصَبَّ عَلَيۡهِمۡ رَبُّكَ سَوۡطَ عَذَابٍ ۝١٣

*“[All of] whom oppressed within the lands And increased therein the corruption So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment”* (Sūrat al-Fajr 89:11–13 · trans. Sahih International)

The people of ʿĀd had announced, in the pride of their corrupt power, “Who is stronger than us in power?” (41:15). The law of recompense turned this bodily arrogance into a helplessness for which no example is found in the history of the world. Allah the Exalted imposed this “whip of punishment” on them for seven nights and eight days continuously:

>> سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَبۡعَ لَيَالٖ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومٗاۖ فَتَرَى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ فِيهَا صَرۡعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلٍ خَاوِيَةٖ

*“Which Allah imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees”* (Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah 69:7 · trans. Sahih International)

This was the great scene of Allah’s law of recompense. Those lofty statures, that physical build, those unparalleled constructions (Iram dhāt al-ʿimād) in which they took pride: one single punishment tore them out from within and brought them down upon the earth. None of their strength and none of their lofty buildings could save them from this punishment. In this grave scene of the punishment of extirpation, under the law of separation, Hūd (peace be upon him) and those who believed in him were granted complete deliverance:

>> فَأَنجَيۡنَٰهُ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحۡمَةٖ مِّنَّا وَقَطَعۡنَا دَابِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَاۖ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُؤۡمِنِينَ

*“So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us. And We eliminated those who denied Our signs, and they were not [at all] believers”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:72 · trans. Sahih International)

In this way the destruction of the people of ʿĀd became, for the history of humanity, a living sign of this eternal law of Allah the Exalted: when the proof is complete, then neither material power saves, nor sovereignty, nor great buildings, nor false gods.

### 3. The People of Thamūd (Sayyidunā Ṣāliḥ): The Denial of the Sign and the Terrible Cry

**The first and second conditions: the clear exposition of the truth and the people’s arrogance.** Sayyidunā Ṣāliḥ gave his people a clear call to tawḥīd and to obedience to Allah the Exalted, which was the conclusive proof:

>> وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمۡ صَٰلِحٗاۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم بَيِّنَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمۡ ءَايَةٗۖ فَذَرُوهَا تَأۡكُلۡ فِيٓ أَرۡضِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءٖ فَيَأۡخُذَكُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٞ

*“And to the Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah 's land and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:73 · trans. Sahih International)

Instead of accepting this truth, the people displayed arrogance and the pride of material power, and mocked the believers:

>> قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِمَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡهُمۡ أَتَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّ صَٰلِحٗا مُّرۡسَلٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦۚ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلَ بِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنُونَ

*“Said the eminent ones who were arrogant among his people to those who were oppressed - to those who believed among them, "Do you [actually] know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said, "Indeed we, in that with which he was sent, are believers”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:75 · trans. Sahih International)

**The third condition: warnings, trials (the incident of the she-camel) and the opportunity to return.** This stage of itmām al-ḥujjah was the turning point, when the people demanded a sign and Allah sent a she-camel as a trial: “This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you; so leave her to eat on Allah’s earth” (7:73, quoted above). When they killed this tangible sign, Allah gave them a last warning:

>> فَعَقَرُوهَا فَقَالَ تَمَتَّعُواْ فِي دَارِكُمۡ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٖۖ ذَٰلِكَ وَعۡدٌ غَيۡرُ مَكۡذُوبٖ

*“But they hamstrung her, so he said, "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:65 · trans. Sahih International)

**The fourth condition: “lā yuʾminūn” and the “stubbornness” of final denial.** At this stage their obstinacy reached such a point that, instead of bringing faith, they challenged the messenger to bring the punishment. This was the peak of their “lā yuʾminūn”:

>> فَعَقَرُواْ ٱلنَّاقَةَ وَعَتَوۡاْ عَنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَقَالُواْ يَٰصَٰلِحُ ٱئۡتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ

*“So they hamstrung the she-camel and were insolent toward the command of their Lord and said, "O Salih, bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the messengers”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:77 · trans. Sahih International)

When three days passed and they stayed fixed in their obstinacy, the divine punishment descended:

>> فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ فِي دَارِهِمۡ جَٰثِمِينَ

*“So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:78 · trans. Sahih International)

### 4. The People of Lūṭ: The Punishment of Moral Depravity and the Stoning

**The first condition: the clear exposition of the truth and the establishment of the proof.** Lūṭ called his people to natural moral purity along with tawḥīd:

>> وَلُوطًا إِذۡ قَالَ لِقَوۡمِهِۦٓ أَتَأۡتُونَ ٱلۡفَٰحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنۡ أَحَدٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ

*“And [We had sent] Lot when he said to his people, "Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:80 · trans. Sahih International)

He closed off the people’s excuse by stating, with complete rational and legal explicitness, the truth against indecency.

**The second condition: the people’s wrongdoing, corruption and deviation from reform.** The people crossed the natural limits and set up the worst example of fasād fī al-arḍ, and they descended to insulting the messenger:

>> ۞فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓاْ أَخۡرِجُوٓاْ ءَالَ لُوطٖ مِّن قَرۡيَتِكُمۡۖ إِنَّهُمۡ أُنَاسٞ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ

*“But the answer of his people was not except that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure”* (Sūrat al-Naml 27:56 · trans. Sahih International)

Mocking purity and threatening to expel the messenger from the town was the proof of their decisive wrongdoing and corruption.

**The third condition: warnings, trials and the opportunity to return.** Lūṭ warned them of the consequences, but his people regarded the warnings with doubt:

>> وَلَقَدۡ أَنذَرَهُم بَطۡشَتَنَا فَتَمَارَوۡاْ بِٱلنُّذُرِ

*“And he had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warning”* (Sūrat al-Qamar 54:36 · trans. Sahih International)

The coming of the angels in human form, and the people’s attempt to attack them, was the last trial, which proved that no trace of good was left in them.

**The fourth condition: “lā yuʾminūn”: decisive denial and the punishment of extirpation.** When the people of the town did not desist from rebellion and the possibility of faith had ended, Allah’s punishment came at morning time:

>> فَجَعَلۡنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمۡطَرۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ حِجَارَةٗ مِّن سِجِّيلٍ

*“And We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of hard clay”* (Sūrat al-Ḥijr 15:74 · trans. Sahih International)

The town was overturned, and stones marked with the name of each person were rained upon it, except for the believers, whom He took out during the night.

### 5. The People of Shuʿayb: Economic Dishonesty and the Seizure of the Earthquake

**The first condition: the clear exposition of the truth and the establishment of the proof.** Shuʿayb gave the people of Madyan a detailed call to tawḥīd and to economic justice (honesty in weights and measures):

>> ۞أَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَلَا تَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡمُخۡسِرِينَ

*“Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss”* (Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:181 · trans. Sahih International)

He made it clear that blessing lies in lawful provision, and he explained the truth with full explicitness.

**The second condition: the people’s wrongdoing, corruption and deviation from reform.** The people mocked him, and made economic corruption their liberty:

>> قَالُواْ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأۡمُرُكَ أَن نَّتۡرُكَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوۡ أَن نَّفۡعَلَ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَـٰٓؤُاْۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلۡحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ

*“They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:87 · trans. Sahih International)

They began to frighten people and to prevent them from the path of Allah, which was the peak of social and economic oppression.

**The third condition: warnings, trials and the opportunity to return.** Shuʿayb warned them with the end of the earlier destroyed peoples (Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Lūṭ), so that they might take the lesson:

>> وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شِقَاقِيٓ أَن يُصِيبَكُم مِّثۡلُ مَآ أَصَابَ قَوۡمَ نُوحٍ أَوۡ قَوۡمَ هُودٍ أَوۡ قَوۡمَ صَٰلِحٖۚ وَمَا قَوۡمُ لُوطٖ مِّنكُم بِبَعِيدٖ

*“And O my people, let not [your] dissension from me cause you to be struck by that similar to what struck the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih. And the people of Lot are not from you far away”* (Sūrat Hūd 11:89 · trans. Sahih International)

They were given continual reminders and opportunities for repentance, so that they might correct their economic conduct.

**The fourth condition: “lā yuʾminūn”: decisive denial and the punishment of extirpation.** When the proof was complete and the people made the decisive decision to expel Shuʿayb from his homeland, Allah’s punishment came in the form of “the day of the shadow” (yawm al-ẓulla):

>> فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمۡ عَذَابُ يَوۡمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمٍ

*“And they denied him, so the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day”* (Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:189 · trans. Sahih International)

Fire rained from a cloud, and then a severe earthquake left them lying in their homes as if they had never lived there.

### 6. The People of Pharaoh: Political Arrogance and the End of Drowning

**The first condition: the clear exposition of the truth and the establishment of the proof.** Sayyidunā Mūsā, going into the court of Pharaoh, conveyed the message of tawḥīd through the perfection of eloquence and powerful miracles (the staff and the white hand):

>> فَلَمَّا جَآءَتۡهُمۡ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبۡصِرَةٗ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا سِحۡرٞ مُّبِينٞ

*“But when there came to them Our visible signs, they said, "This is obvious magic”* (Sūrat al-Naml 27:13 · trans. Sahih International)

The open acceptance of faith by the magicians shook the political foundations of Pharaoh and completed the proof.

**The second condition: the people’s wrongdoing, corruption and deviation from reform.** Pharaoh raised the slogan “I am your lord, the most high” and carried political arrogance to its limit:

>> إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ وَكَانُواْ قَوۡمًا عَالِينَ

*“To Pharaoh and his establishment, but they were arrogant and were a haughty people”* (Sūrat al-Muʾminūn 23:46 · trans. Sahih International)

The killing of the sons of Banī Isrāʾīl, the keeping alive of their women, and the forced denial of the call of truth was the great wrongdoing that stood the town at the brink of destruction.

**The third condition: warnings, trials and the opportunity to return.** Allah tried the family of Pharaoh with nine successive warnings (the flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood and others):

>> فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلۡجَرَادَ وَٱلۡقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَٰتٖ مُّفَصَّلَٰتٖ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ وَكَانُواْ قَوۡمٗا مُّجۡرِمِينَ

*“So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:133 · trans. Sahih International)

At every punishment they would beg Mūsā to pray, but when the relief came they would break their promise again. This was a sign of their decisive rebellion.

**The fourth condition: “lā yuʾminūn”: decisive denial and the punishment of extirpation.** When every possibility of guidance was over, then by the command of Allah the sea became their end:

>> فَٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡهَا غَٰفِلِينَ

*“So We took retribution from them, and We drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them”* (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:136 · trans. Sahih International)

The faith of Pharaoh at the last moment was rejected, and he was made a sign of lesson for the generations to come.

### 7. The People of Ibrāhīm: The Completion of Rational Proof and the Migration of the Messenger

**The first condition: the clear exposition of the truth and the establishment of the proof.** Sayyidunā Ibrāhīm made the truth completely clear to his people through rational arguments and through the observations and scenes of the natural disposition (fiṭrah):

>> وَتِلۡكَ حُجَّتُنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦۚ نَرۡفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٖ مَّن نَّشَآءُۗ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٞ

*“And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing”* (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:83 · trans. Sahih International)

Breaking the idols and presenting practical proof of their helplessness was the last stage of the conclusive proof.

**The second condition: the people’s wrongdoing, corruption and deviation from reform.** When the people had no answer to the argument, they chose the path of the worst wrongdoing:

>> قَالُواْ ٱبۡنُواْ لَهُۥ بُنۡيَٰنٗا فَأَلۡقُوهُ فِي ٱلۡجَحِيمِ

*“They said, "Construct for him a furnace and throw him into the burning fire”* (Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt 37:97 · trans. Sahih International)

This conduct of theirs was an attempt to suppress the truth by force, which, after itmām al-ḥujjah, becomes a cause of destruction.

**The third condition: warnings, trials and the opportunity to return.** The fire becoming cool and safe for Ibrāhīm was one of the greatest signs and the last warning:

>> قُلۡنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِي بَرۡدٗا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ

*“Allah said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham”* (Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ 21:69 · trans. Sahih International)

By this clear miracle the truth was proved against them to such a degree that not to believe now meant only destruction.

**The fourth condition: “lā yuʾminūn”: decisive denial and the punishment of extirpation.** When, even after this miracle, they remained fixed in disbelief, Ibrāhīm announced his migration (37:99). The mention of them together with the destroyed peoples in Sūrat al-Tawbah (9:70) is proof that they were afflicted by Allah’s punishment as recompense for their decisive denial, after which their name and trace were wiped out.

## The Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ, the Completion of Proof and the General Mercy of Allah

### 1. The Four Stages of Itmām al-Ḥujjah in the Blessed Life of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

In the Makkan life of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (before the hijrah), Allah the Exalted, in accordance with the sunnah of the earlier peoples, fulfilled all the requirements of itmām al-ḥujjah. The summary is as follows:

1. **Clear exposition of the truth (the truth being made clear):** The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to tawḥīd in Makkah for 13 years with such clarity and transparency that no room for excuse remained for anyone. Allah the Exalted said:

>> قُلۡ أَيُّ شَيۡءٍ أَكۡبَرُ شَهَٰدَةٗۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ شَهِيدُۢ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكُمۡۚ وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ لِأُنذِرَكُم بِهِۦ وَمَنۢ بَلَغَۚ أَئِنَّكُمۡ لَتَشۡهَدُونَ أَنَّ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ ءَالِهَةً أُخۡرَىٰۚ قُل لَّآ أَشۡهَدُۚ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَٰهٞ وَٰحِدٞ وَإِنَّنِي بَرِيٓءٞ مِّمَّا تُشۡرِكُونَ

*“Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you [truly] testify that with Allah there are other deities?" Say, "I will not testify [with you]." Say, "Indeed, He is but one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate [with Him]”* (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:19 · trans. Sahih International)

2. **Corruption and the denial of the call of truth:** When the truth became clear, the polytheists of Makkah chose the path of stubbornness, arrogance and wrongdoing. They not only denied the call of truth themselves. They also took recourse to noise, clamour and propaganda to suppress it. The Qur’an describes this behaviour in these words:

>> وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَا تَسۡمَعُواْ لِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَٱلۡغَوۡاْ فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَغۡلِبُونَ

*“And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an and speak noisily during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome”* (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:26 · trans. Sahih International)

3. **Warnings and trials (the lesser punishment):** Before the hijrah, the polytheists of Makkah were warned through various warnings and smaller seizures (famine and the like), so that they might adopt humility. Allah the Exalted said:

>> فَٱرۡتَقِبۡ يَوۡمَ تَأۡتِي ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٖ مُّبِينٖ

*“Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke”* (Sūrat al-Dukhān 44:10 · trans. Sahih International)

4. **“Lā yuʾminūn” and the final state:** Continuous denial and obstinacy produced in their hearts a state in which the possibility of faith had ended, as is mentioned in Sūrat al-Baqarah:

>> إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ

*“Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe”* (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:6 · trans. Sahih International)

### 2. The Special Dealing with the Polytheists of Makkah: The Sword and Conquest as Divine Punishment

In the earlier peoples, after itmām al-ḥujjah, Allah the Exalted mostly carried out the punishment of extirpation through heavenly punishment (the flood, an earthquake or a rain of stones). But for this ummah, Allah the Exalted made the sword and conquest the means of carrying out this divine sunnah. In the case of the polytheists of Makkah, the final result of itmām al-ḥujjah appeared in the form of the “dominance of truth” and the conquest of Makkah, instead of the “punishment of extirpation”.

This was the stage at which, after all the warnings and itmām al-ḥujjah, they refused even then to accept the truth. Then Allah the Exalted commanded the Muslims that this punishment would now descend upon them at their hands:

>> قَٰتِلُوهُمۡ يُعَذِّبۡهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ وَيُخۡزِهِمۡ وَيَنصُرۡكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَيَشۡفِ صُدُورَ قَوۡمٖ مُّؤۡمِنِينَ

*“Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people”* (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:14 · trans. Sahih International)

The meaning of “yuʿadhdhibhumu Allāhu bi-aydīkum” (“Allah will punish them by your hands”) in this verse is extremely deep. It means that itmām al-ḥujjah has now been completed, and that this is the divine punishment which is descending upon them through the hands of the Muslims.

### The Conquest of Makkah: The Logical Result of Itmām al-Ḥujjah

The conquest of Makkah was not merely a military success. It was that historical peak of itmām al-ḥujjah at which the last fortress of disbelief was demolished. This conquest proved that when the proof is established completely, Allah the Exalted grants dominance to His religion:

>> هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ رَسُولَهُۥ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلۡحَقِّ لِيُظۡهِرَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِۦۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدٗا

*“It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as Witness”* (Sūrat al-Fatḥ 48:28 · trans. Sahih International)

This conquest was in reality the logical result of these four stages. When the polytheists of Makkah crossed all the limits of wrongdoing and oppression, the dominance of truth, through the sword, fell upon them as “divine punishment” and cut off the roots of shirk and corruption.

### The Requirements of Itmām al-Ḥujjah in the Present Age and the Human Responsibility

Although the principle of general warning (indhār ʿāmm) still exists, its application in the present age demands the utmost caution and strict adherence to the Qur’anic standards. In the present circumstances, the basic responsibility of human beings is to convey the truth to others in a correct and clear manner. It is not to issue fatwas about itmām al-ḥujjah upon peoples, nor to announce divine decisions about them. The knowledge that the proof is complete upon any people lies only with Allah. Therefore the work of the caller is only clear conveyance (balāgh mubīn).

In the matter of the general warning, and of non-Muslim individuals of the present age, the noble Qur’an describes two different aspects separately. One is that a people should be established upon as a group proof. The other is that each individual should be reckoned with according to his own knowledge. The demand of Allah’s mercy is that a warner be sent to every ummah (Fāṭir 35:24), and the principle of punishment is the one stated in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ (17:15): “And We never punish until We send a messenger.” Here, the arrival of the messenger is not the mere hearing of a name. It is the clarity of the truth to such a degree that no excuse remains for man. The Qur’an also states plainly that all groups of the People of the Book are not alike (Āl ʿImrān 3:113), and that the final decision of guidance rests with the knowledge and wisdom of Allah (al-Qaṣaṣ 28:56). Therefore the application of the social sunnah concerns the conduct of societies, while the reckoning of individuals is wholly with the perfect justice of Allah. In the present age, to claim itmām al-ḥujjah upon any society is an extremely sensitive matter, for which the wise Qur’an has set strict standards. According to Sūrat Ibrāhīm (14:4), the condition of conveyance is that it be in “lisān qawmihi” (the tongue of the people), so that it may become fully clear. Since the final decision whether the proof is complete lies only in Allah’s authority (al-Ḥajj 22:69), our duty at the human level is only to call and to make the truth clear, in the manner of the prophets. To leave the decisive judgement about the destruction of a people, or about the completion of the proof upon them, to Allah’s attribute of justice and His knowledge of the unseen is itself the demand of Qur’anic wisdom.

## The Fundamental Difference between Itmām al-Ḥujjah and Jihad: A Legal and Qur’anic Analysis

Itmām al-ḥujjah is a divine sunnah whose relation is directly with the will and justice of Allah the Exalted, and it is specific to the prophets. According to the wise Qur’an, before social punishment Allah the Exalted has set four stages of itmām al-ḥujjah (the clear exposition of the truth, the wrongdoing and insistence of the people, warnings and trials, and the state of “lā yuʾminūn”). It is an extremely important and delicate matter at which stage a people stands at present, and when the proof has been completed. The decisive knowledge of this lies only with Allah the Exalted. To declare a people “proof-completed” at the human level, and to demand punishment upon them, is against the spirit of the sharīʿah. In contrast, jihad relates to the ending of the wrongdoing and corruption that is in force on the earth. It does not wait for the stages of itmām al-ḥujjah. It is a practical obligation.

### Clarifying the Concept of Wrongdoing (Ẓulm) and Corruption (Fasād): The Difference between the Settings of the Prophets and of the Peoples

It is necessary to understand that in the wise Qur’an the word “ẓulm” is used in two different contexts, and their application is different:

1. **For the noble prophets:** When this word appears about the prophets (for example, with reference to Yūnus, “innī kuntu min al-ẓālimīn”), what is meant is not any moral corruption or disobedience of the sharīʿah. It is the expression of spiritual humility and servanthood before Allah. This reflects their high station of taqwā, where they describe even some ordinary shortcoming as “ẓulm” (wronging one’s own self).
2. **For the peoples:** In the context of divine punishment, “ẓulm” means “social rebellion”, “fasād fī al-arḍ” and the deliberate denial of the truth. This is the wrongdoing that destroys social peace and becomes the cause of Allah’s seizure.
