7. **Manifested in relieving hardship.** It removes burdens people could otherwise bear only "with difficulty to yourselves" (16:7). It also shows in subjecting the earth, ships, and sky for human benefit (22:65).

8. **Manifested in protecting faith.** "Never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith" (2:143). He turns in forgiveness to those whose hearts "had almost inclined [to doubt]" (9:117).

9. **Manifested in guidance.** He sends down clear verses "that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light" (57:9).

10. **Present even within warning and threat.** It is mentioned directly after "Allah warns you of Himself" (3:30) and after the possibility of being seized "gradually [in a state of dread]" (16:47). The warning and the respite are thereby framed within His kindness.

11. **Responsive to devotion.** It is mentioned after describing one who "sells himself, seeking means to the approval of Allah" (2:207).

12. **A ground of rescue from consequence.** "If it had not been for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy... and because Allah is Kind and Merciful" (24:20) presents His kindness as a reason harm was averted.

13. **A basis for supplication.** Believers address Him by this attribute when asking forgiveness and purity of heart (59:10). It is therefore an attribute to be called upon, not only described.

14. **Shared in name, distinct in reality.** The same word describes the Messenger (9:128). The data, however, shows his kindness as limited in scope ("to the believers") and expressed as grief and concern. Allah's kindness is universal and expressed through creation, guidance, forgiveness, and respite.

### Limits of the Data
The texts do not define رَءُوف lexically. They also do not state explicitly how it differs in meaning from رَحِيم. Any distinction between the two beyond the contextual patterns noted above cannot be established from the data provided.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The lemma يَتَفَكَّرُ (root ف ك ر) occurs **17 times in 12 surahs**: 12 times in Makki surahs and 5 times in Madani surahs. It always appears as an imperfect plural verb, in five surface forms: يتفكرون ×10, تتفكرون ×3, يتفكروا ×2, ويتفكرون ×1 and تتفكروا ×1. The third-person forms (13 occurrences) clearly outnumber the second-person forms (4 occurrences). In most places the verb has no expressed object. Only twice is the object of reflection named, each time with فِي. The four groups below are based on the construction and context in which the verb appears.

### Signs in creation for "a people who give thought"

Here the verb ends a fixed formula. A description of natural or human phenomena is followed by the statement that these contain a sign or signs for a people who reflect:

>> إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتٖ لِّقَوۡمٖ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

In 13:3 this is rendered "Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought."

The subjects of the signs vary:
- the spreading of the earth, its mountains, rivers and paired fruits (13:3)
- the growth of crops and fruit (16:11)
- the bee's drink "in which there is healing for people" (16:69)
- the creation of mates with "affection and mercy" (30:21)
- the taking of souls in death and sleep (39:42)
- the subjection of "whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" (45:13)

The verb describes a category of people, لِّقَوۡمٖ, who are the intended beneficiaries of the sign. It is not addressed to an audience directly.

**References:** 13:3, 16:11, 16:69, 30:21, 39:42, 45:13

### Revelation, parables and stories set out so that people might reflect

In this group, reflection is the hoped-for result of divine explanation, parable or narrative. The verb usually follows لَعَلَّ:

>> كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ

In 2:219 this is rendered "Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses [of revelation] that you might give thought."

The verb is paired with verbs of clarifying and setting out:
- يُبَيِّنُ (2:219, 2:266)
- لِتُبَيِّنَ (16:44)
- ٱقۡصُصِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ (7:176)
- ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلُ نَضۡرِبُهَا (59:21)

Several of these passages are similitudes: the burned garden (2:266), the panting dog (7:176), and the Qur'an sent down on a mountain (59:21).

The placement of 10:24 is less certain. It shares the لِقَوۡمٖ construction of the first group:

>> كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمٖ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

The data renders this "Thus do We explain in detail the signs for a people who give thought." However, its content is a parable ("The example of [this] worldly life is but like rain...") introduced by a verb of explaining, which aligns it with this group.

**References:** 2:219, 2:266, 7:176, 10:24, 16:44, 59:21

### Reproach and exhortation concerning the Messenger and his message

Here the verb occurs in rhetorical questions or commands directed at those who reject the message. The object of the reflection is the Messenger's status or the truth he brings.

In 6:50 a comparison is followed by a reproachful question:

>> قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡبَصِيرُۚ أَفَلَا تَتَفَكَّرُونَ

This is rendered "Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Then will you not give thought.'"

Two passages are closely parallel. Both lead directly to the denial of madness in "their/your companion" and to his description as a warner:

>> أَوَلَمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُواْۗ مَا بِصَاحِبِهِم مِّن جِنَّةٍۚ

>> ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُواْۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍۚ

The first (7:184) is rendered "Then do they not give thought? There is in their companion [Muhammad] no madness." The second (34:46) is rendered "...and then give thought." There is not in your companion any madness.

The verse 30:8 shares the أَوَلَمۡ question:

>> أَوَلَمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۗ

This is rendered "Do they not contemplate within themselves?" It is placed here with some hesitation. Its content, that creation is "in truth and for a specified term," overlaps with the creation group, while its framing as a reproach of those who are disbelievers in "the meeting with their Lord" aligns it with this group.

**References:** 6:50, 7:184, 30:8, 34:46

### Reflection as a mark of the devout

In one place the verb describes the conduct of believers rather than the purpose of a sign or a reproach. It is coordinated with remembrance of God and takes an explicit object:

>> ٱلَّذِينَ يَذۡكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَٰمٗا وَقُعُودٗا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمۡ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ

This is rendered "Who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth."

The reflection leads directly into a prayer: "Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly." This is the only occurrence where the outcome of reflecting is voiced by those who reflect.

**References:** 3:191

## Patterns worth a researcher's attention

- **Forms without the final nūn are restricted to the reproach group.** They are يَتَفَكَّرُواْ (7:184, 30:8), following أَوَلَمۡ, and تَتَفَكَّرُواْ (34:46), following ثُمَّ in coordination with أَن تَقُومُواْ. All three are Makki.
- **The لِقَوۡمٖ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ formula is predominantly Makki.** Of its six occurrences with إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ, five are Makki, and 13:3 is labelled Madani in the data. Within the formula, the singular لَأٓيَةٗ appears only in surah 16 (16:11, 16:69). Elsewhere the plural لَأٓيَٰتٖ is used (13:3, 30:21, 39:42, 45:13).
- **The second-person forms address the audience directly.** In the two Madani verses 2:219 and 2:266, the identical clause كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ closes passages on legal questions and on a parable. The Makki second-person forms (6:50, 34:46) are confrontational instead.
- **لَعَلَّ + verb** occurs five times (2:219, 2:266, 7:176, 16:44, 59:21). It is consistently tied to revelation, clarification, stories or parables, never to the natural signs of the first group.
- **The verb takes an explicit object only twice,** both times with فِي: فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ (3:191) and فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۗ (30:8). Both concern the creation of the heavens and the earth. Elsewhere the object is left implicit or supplied by ذَٰلِكَ.
- **Several collocations recur across groups:**
  - the phrase مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ (2:266, 13:3, 16:11, 16:69)
  - palm trees and grapevines (2:266 نَخِيلٖ وَأَعۡنَٰبٖ; 16:11 ٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَٰبَ)
  - أَجَلٖ مُّسَمّٗى / مُّسَمًّى (30:8, 39:42)
  - forms of أَنفُس (30:8, 30:21, 39:42)
- **Agricultural imagery serves opposite purposes.** In 2:266 and 10:24 abundant vegetation is shown destroyed as a warning image. In 13:3 and 16:11 it is presented as a sign of provision.

## The use in 16:11

In 16:11, يَتَفَكَّرُونَ belongs squarely to the first group, signs in creation for a people who give thought:

>> إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةٗ لِّقَوۡمٖ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

This is rendered "Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought." The sign is the growing of "the crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and from all the fruits." The pronoun in بِهِ ("thereby") refers to something outside the quoted ayah, which the data does not supply.

Three features distinguish this occurrence:
- It shares the singular لَأٓيَةٗ only with 16:69, in the same surah.
- It shares the phrase مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ with 2:266, 13:3 and 16:69. Of these, 13:3 is closest to it in content and construction.
- Its pairing of palm trees and grapevines also appears in the parable of 2:266. There the same produce is destroyed to prompt reflection, whereas here it flourishes as a sign of provision.

The verb in 16:11 thus describes a disposition attributed to a category of people. It is not an exhortation addressed to them, and the object of their reflection is the provision drawn from the earth.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The lemma أَلْقَى (root ل ق ي) occurs **71 times in 30 surahs**: 58 in Makki surahs and 13 in Madani surahs. Its forms cover the perfect, the imperfect, the imperative and the passive. The most frequent are القى (×9), القوا (×8), يلقى (×6) and فالقى (×5). They are followed by والقينا and والقى (×4 each), فالقوا (×3), and يلقون, سنلقى, والقوا, تلقى, الق, فالقوه and والق (×2 each). Fifteen further forms occur once each, including the dual imperatives القيا and فالقياه and the interrogative passive اءلقى. The translations render the verb in many ways: "throw", "cast", "offer", "deliver", "place", "convey", "present", "impart", "pass on", "listens", "fell down". This range shows a single core action, setting something down or sending it forth, extended to physical, psychological, verbal and cosmic objects.

### Moses' staff and the contest with the magicians

This is the largest and most uniform group. It contains the divine command to Moses to throw his staff, its transformation, and the exchange of "throwing" between Moses and Pharaoh's magicians. The object is concrete: a staff, or ropes and staffs. The act is typically followed by a sudden result introduced by فَإِذَا. Moses' throw is contrasted with the magicians' throw. Their act produces magic that "bewitched the eyes of the people". His staff "devoured what they falsified":
>> فَأَلۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلۡقَفُ مَا يَأۡفِكُونَ
"Then Moses threw his staff, and at once it devoured what they falsified" (26:45).

- 7:107, 7:115, 7:116 (×2), 7:117, 10:80, 10:81, 20:19, 20:20, 20:65 (×2), 20:66, 20:69, 26:32, 26:43, 26:44, 26:45, 27:10, 28:31

### The magicians "thrown down" in prostration

In these three verses the verb is passive and the magicians are its grammatical subject. The agent is unstated. The translation renders it as an intransitive "fell down", while the gloss at 20:70 keeps "were thrown down". The verb is always paired with a word of prostration (سَٰجِدِينَ or سُجَّدٗا). It closes the contest above by turning the throwers into those who are themselves cast down:
>> فَأُلۡقِيَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
"So the magicians fell down in prostration [to Allah]" (26:46).

- 7:120, 20:70, 26:46

### Throwing objects and persons in other narratives

Here the verb denotes physically throwing or placing something in the course of a narrative:
- pens cast to decide guardianship of Mary;
- the tablets thrown down by Moses in anger;
- Joseph thrown into the well;
- Joseph's shirt cast over his father's face;
- the infant Moses cast into the river, and the river casting him onto the bank;
- the Samiri's throwing;
- Abraham thrown into the fire.

The prepositions mark destination: في for an enclosure (well, river, fire) and على for a surface (face). The agents range widely: brothers, a mother, a river, idolaters, Moses himself. At 20:87 the object of the Samiri's throwing is not stated in the ayah, so what he threw cannot be determined from the text given.

- 3:44, 7:150, 12:10, 12:93, 12:96, 20:39 (فَلۡيُلۡقِهِ), 20:87, 28:7, 37:97

### Casting into Hell, the Fire, and destruction

In this group people are cast into Hell, the Fire, the "severe punishment" or a narrow place within it. Most occurrences are passive (أُلۡقُواْ, أُلۡقِيَ, يُلۡقَىٰ, تُلۡقَىٰ) or dual imperatives addressed to unnamed agents (أَلۡقِيَا, فَأَلۡقِيَاهُ). Those described are disbelievers and those who associate another deity with Allah. 41:40 sets this casting against the one "who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection". I include 2:195 here as a related, reflexive use: believers are told not to cast themselves into destruction.
>> وَلَا تُلۡقُواْ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلتَّهۡلُكَةِ
"do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands into destruction [by refraining]" (2:195).

- 2:195, 17:39, 25:13, 41:40, 50:24, 50:26, 67:7, 67:8

### Mountains cast into the earth, and what the earth casts out

In four verses Allah is the agent who casts "firmly set mountains" (رَوَٰسِيَ) into the earth. The verb is consistently paired with other acts of creation: spreading out the earth, causing vegetation to grow, dispersing creatures, and creating the heavens without pillars:
>> وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَدَدۡنَٰهَا وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ
(15:19)

84:4 is placed here tentatively. It describes something feminine that "has cast out that within it and relinquished [it]". Since the ayah itself names neither the subject nor its contents, identifying the subject as the earth is uncertain on the data given.

- 15:19, 16:15, 31:10, 50:7, 84:4

### Allah casting states, emotions and trials upon people

Here the object is abstract: terror into the hearts of disbelievers, animosity and hatred among a people, and love bestowed upon Moses. One verse has a body placed on Solomon's throne as part of a trial. The prepositions are في قلوب, بين and على.
>> سَنُلۡقِي فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلرُّعۡبَ
"We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve" (3:151).

At 38:34 the object جَسَدٗا is concrete, but the verse frames it as part of a divine trial (فَتَنَّا). Its exact sense is not clarified by the text.

- 3:151, 5:64, 8:12, 20:39 (وَأَلۡقَيۡتُ), 38:34

### Conveying revelation, a word, or a letter

The object is a word, inspiration, a book, a message or a letter. It is delivered to or upon a recipient with إلى or على. Allah is the sender in 4:171 (His word to Mary), 40:15 (the inspiration of His command) and 73:5. In the latter the casting of "a heavy word" is set out as a promise:
>> إِنَّا سَنُلۡقِي عَلَيۡكَ قَوۡلٗا ثَقِيلًا
"Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word" (73:5).

In 27:28 and 27:29 the object is Solomon's letter delivered to the Queen. In 54:25 opponents ask, in disbelief, whether the message has been sent down upon a man from among them.

- 4:171, 27:28, 27:29, 28:86, 40:15, 54:25, 73:5

### Material signs demanded of a messenger

In two verses opponents demand that something be cast down to or upon a messenger as proof: a treasure, or bracelets of gold. Both are passive and both occur in objection speech. They resemble the revelation group in structure (passive verb with إلى or على), but the object is wealth rather than a message.

- 25:8, 43:53

### Offering peace, submission, affection, words or excuses

Here the verb denotes extending a stance or utterance toward another party, usually with إلى. The most frequent object is السَّلَم ("peace" or "submission"), and once السَّلَٰمَ. In surah 4 it is offered by non-combatants to believers in a context of fighting:
>> وَأَلۡقَوۡاْ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلسَّلَمَ
"offer you peace" (4:90).

In 16:28 and 16:87 the wrongdoers offer submission at death and on the Day. In 16:86 the "partners" throw back a statement. In 60:1 believers extend affection to enemies, and in 75:15 a person presents his excuses.

- 4:90, 4:91, 4:94, 16:28, 16:86, 16:87, 60:1, 75:15

### "Casting the hearing": listening and passing on what is heard

With the object ٱلسَّمۡعَ the verb denotes directing hearing. In 50:37 this is attentive listening: "who listens while he is present [in mind]". In 26:223 it is rendered "They pass on what is heard", said of those of whom "most of them are liars". The same phrase thus bears opposite moral valuations. Whether 26:223 means listening or transmitting is uncertain on the text alone; the translation chooses transmission.
>> أَوۡ أَلۡقَى ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٞ
(50:37)

- 26:223, 50:37

### What Satan casts in

In 22:52–53 Satan is the agent. He casts something into a messenger's or prophet's أُمۡنِيَّة: "Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding]". Allah's acts answer his: He "abolishes" what Satan throws in, "makes precise His verses", and makes it a trial for the sick-hearted. What exactly is cast is not stated; the bracketed "[some misunderstanding]" is the translation's supplement.

- 22:52 (×2), 22:53

## Patterns worth a researcher's attention

- **Prepositional frames correlate with sense.**
  - **إلى + addressee** marks conveying or offering: peace, submission, a letter, the Book, a word, affection.
  - **في + place** marks casting into a container or domain: the earth, Hell, a well, the river, hearts.
  - **على + surface or person** marks placing upon: a face, a throne, a messenger, a heavy word.
- **The passive** (أُلۡقِيَ, أُلۡقُواْ, يُلۡقَىٰ, تُلۡقَىٰ, أَءُلۡقِيَ) is concentrated in three settings:
  - the magicians' prostration (7:120, 20:70, 26:46);
  - casting into Hell (17:39, 25:13, 41:40, 67:7, 67:8);
  - things sent to a messenger or recipient (25:8, 27:29, 28:86, 43:53, 54:25).
- **The imperative** clusters in the Moses narratives (أَلۡقِ, أَلۡقُواْ, أَلۡقِهَا) and in the dual commands of Hell (50:24, 50:26).
- **The mountains collocation** رَوَٰسِيَ + في الأرض/فيها is fixed in all four creation verses, all Makki. It occurs in two parallel shapes:
  - first person plural وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا with مَدَدۡنَٰهَا and أَنۢبَتۡنَا (15:19, 50:7);
  - third person singular وَأَلۡقَىٰ with the purpose clause أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمۡ (16:15, 31:10).
- **Makki and Madani distribution.**
  - Entirely Makki: the staff narratives, the Hell scenes, the mountains, and the "casting the hearing" phrase.
  - The Madani occurrences gather around warfare and community relations: terror cast into hearts (3:151, 8:12), peace offered in fighting contexts (4:90, 4:91, 4:94), animosity cast among a people (5:64), affection extended to enemies (60:1), and self-destruction (2:195). Satan's casting (22:52–53) and the word to Mary (4:171) are the other Madani uses.
- **The السَّلَم collocation** spans both periods with different settings. In Madani surah 4 peace is offered to believers. In Makki surah 16 submission is offered by wrongdoers at death and to Allah on the Day.
- **Surah 16 concentrates the range.** It contains four occurrences in contrasting senses: cosmic (16:15), submission at death (16:28), a statement thrown back (16:86), and submission on the Day (16:87).

## The use in 16:15

>> وَأَلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٰسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمۡ وَأَنۡهَٰرٗا وَسُبُلٗا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
"And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shift with you, and [made] rivers and roads, that you may be guided"

The occurrence at 16:15 belongs to the creation group. Allah is the agent, the frame is في + place, and the object is the fixed term رَوَٰسِيَ. Its closest parallel is 31:10, which repeats وَأَلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٰسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمۡ almost verbatim. 15:19 and 50:7 express the same act in the first person plural. Within the lemma's wider range, the verse shares with the narrative groups the concrete image of placing a physical object into a location. It shares with the divine-agent groups (terror, love, revelation) the sense of an act performed from above upon a recipient. The verse itself adds two distinctive features. It states a purpose, preventing the earth from shifting. It also extends the object beyond mountains to "rivers and roads" toward a goal of guidance, "that you may be guided". Whether "[made]" is implied for rivers and roads, or whether وَأَلۡقَىٰ governs them directly, is not settled by the text; the bracket marks it as the translation's supplement.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The lemma طاغُوت (root ط غ ي) occurs **8 times in 5 surahs**. Two occurrences are in Makki surahs (16:36, 39:17) and six in Madani surahs (2:256, 2:257, 4:51, 4:60, 4:76, 5:60). The word always carries the definite article. It appears bare as الطغوت six times, with the preposition bi- as بالطغوت once (2:256), and with the conjunction wa- as والطغوت once (4:51). The translation used here mostly leaves the word as "Taghut." The exceptions are 4:51, rendered "false objects of worship," and 5:60, where the phrase is rendered "slaves of Taghut." The word-by-word glosses range across "false deities," "false gods," and "the evil ones."

### Object of worship to be avoided

Here the word names whatever is worshipped in place of Allah. The command, or the commendation, is to keep away from it. It is set directly against the worship of Allah, or against turning back to Allah, and the verb اجتنب ("avoid") governs it in both cases where that verb appears. In 5:60 the word is the object of the verb عَبَدَ. The ayah describes people under curse and anger, and the translation renders the phrase "slaves of Taghut." The grammatical construal of عَبَدَ in that ayah should be treated with some caution.

>> أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱجۡتَنِبُواْ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتَۖ

>> وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱجۡتَنَبُواْ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتَ أَن يَعۡبُدُوهَا

>> وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتَۚ

- 5:60, 16:36, 39:17

### Object of belief or disbelief

Here the word is the object of the verbs of faith and unbelief, كفر بـ and آمن بـ. In 2:256, disbelieving in Taghut is paired with believing in Allah, and together they amount to having "grasped the most trustworthy handhold." In 4:51 the word is coordinated with الجبت ("superstition" in the translation) as something believed in by "those who were given a portion of the Scripture." In 4:60 the people described "were commanded to reject it," which uses the same verb كفر بـ.

>> فَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِٱلطَّـٰغُوتِ وَيُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ

>> يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡجِبۡتِ وَٱلطَّـٰغُوتِ

- 2:256, 4:51, 4:60

### Rival authority for judgment

In 4:60 the word also names an authority to which people seek to take their disputes. The translation renders this as wishing "to refer legislation to Taghut." These people "claim to have believed" in what was revealed. In the same ayah, Satan wishes "to lead them far astray." The data does not settle whether the word here refers to a person, an institution, or a principle.

>> يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَتَحَاكَمُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّـٰغُوتِ وَقَدۡ أُمِرُوٓاْ أَن يَكۡفُرُواْ بِهِۦۖ

- 4:60

### Patron and cause of the disbelievers

Here the word stands for an active agent or cause on the side of those who disbelieve, in deliberate parallel with Allah on the side of the believers. In 2:257 Allah is the ally who brings believers "from darknesses into the light," whereas for the disbelievers "their allies are Taghut. They take them out of the light into darknesses." In 4:76 the disbelievers "fight in the cause of Taghut," as against fighting "in the cause of Allah." The ayah then names their side "the allies of Satan."

>> وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآؤُهُمُ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتُ يُخۡرِجُونَهُم مِّنَ ٱلنُّورِ إِلَى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ

>> وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتِ

- 2:257, 4:76

## Patterns worth a researcher's attention

- **Makki versus Madani.** Both Makki occurrences (16:36, 39:17) share one construction: the verb اجتنب with the word as its direct object, set in the context of worship (اعبدوا الله / أن يعبدوها). The Madani occurrences are more varied. They show the word as the object of belief or disbelief, as a source of judgment, as a patron (أولياء), and as a cause (في سبيل).
- **Systematic contrast with Allah.** In five of the eight occurrences (2:256, 2:257, 4:76, 16:36, 39:17), the word stands in an explicit binary with Allah: disbelieve in Taghut / believe in Allah; Allah as ally / Taghut as allies; the cause of Allah / the cause of Taghut; worship Allah / avoid Taghut; avoid Taghut / turn back to Allah.
- **Association with Satan.** In 4:60 and 4:76 the word appears alongside الشيطان in the same ayah. In 4:76 the opponents fighting "in the cause of Taghut" are then called "the allies of Satan." The data shows close association between the two terms but not full identification.
- **Grammatical agreement.** The word's referential number and gender vary with context. In 2:257 it is followed by a plural verb (يُخۡرِجُونَهُم). In 39:17 it takes a feminine pronoun (يَعۡبُدُوهَا). In 4:60 it takes a masculine singular pronoun (بِهِۦ). This suggests the word can function as a collective or generic term, though the data alone cannot fix its range.
- **Prepositional collocations.** The word occurs with بـ after كفر and آمن (2:256, 4:51, 4:60), with إلى after تحاكم (4:60), and with في سبيل (4:76). Only in the worship-and-avoidance contexts (5:60, 16:36, 39:17) is it a direct object in the accusative.

## The use in 16:36

In 16:36 the word appears in the accusative as the direct object of ٱجۡتَنِبُواْ. It is coordinated with the command ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ, and the translation gives "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut." This places it squarely in the first group, the object of worship to be avoided, and it shares that exact construction with the other Makki occurrence, 39:17. What sets 16:36 apart is its scope. The command is framed as the content of the message sent "into every nation," so avoiding Taghut is presented as a constant of prophetic preaching rather than a matter tied to one community. The ayah's division of people into "those whom Allah guided" and "those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed" echoes the light-and-darkness and guidance-and-error polarities found in the Madani occurrences (2:256, 2:257, 5:60). Read across the corpus, 16:36 can therefore be seen as the basic formulation of the Allah–Taghut opposition that the Madani passages later develop in the vocabulary of belief, allegiance, judgment, and fighting.

## What Taghut is: a conclusion

The usage above supports a definite conclusion about the word's meaning, though one point of scholarly judgment is flagged below. Taghut comes from the root ط غ ي, which carries the sense of transgressing bounds. In the Qur'an it names anything that is obeyed, followed, worshipped, or given ultimate allegiance in place of Allah, and so oversteps the limit proper to a creature. Four findings from the data support this.

1. **It is defined by its relation to Allah, not by one fixed identity.** In the worship contexts (16:36, 39:17) it is what stands against the worship of Allah. In 2:256 disbelief in it is the necessary pair of belief in Allah. In 2:257 and 4:76 it stands opposite Allah as patron and as cause.
2. **It covers more than idols.** It can be something worshipped (5:60), something believed in (4:51), an authority for judgment (4:60), and a patron whose cause people fight for (2:257, 4:76). It is therefore a functional category, defined by what a thing is made to be, and not a single named object.
3. **It can be singular, plural, masculine or feminine in reference** (2:257, 39:17, 4:60). This points to a generic or collective term.
4. **It is closely linked to Satan** (4:60, 4:76) as the one who leads astray, though the text does not simply equate the two.

The conclusion is therefore this: Taghut is any person, power, system, ideology, or object that is given the obedience, authority, or devotion that belongs to Allah alone, and that leads people away from Him. The Qur'an's remedy is the same in every case: reject it and hold to Allah (2:256).

### In the modern context

Applying this definition to today is a matter of interpretation and not something the Qur'anic data fixes. The word's general, functional character is what makes such application possible, and classical and modern scholars have applied it in this way. Following that reading, the things that would count as Taghut are those that meet the criteria the text itself gives:

- **Objects of worship besides Allah.** Idols, and any being or thing treated as divine or as an intercessor with independent power (16:36, 39:17, 5:60).
- **Authorities that claim the right to legislate or judge against Allah's guidance, and that people knowingly turn to in preference to it** (4:60). This is what a person or institution would be if it demanded to be obeyed in contradiction of revelation. It does not cover ordinary governance, law, or administration that does not require disobeying Allah.
- **Ideologies or causes that people give absolute devotion to and fight for as ultimate** (4:76), where that devotion displaces allegiance to Allah.
- **Forces that draw people "out of the light into darknesses"** (2:257): anything that systematically pulls people toward disbelief and away from guidance.

Three cautions apply. First, the text speaks of what is worshipped, believed in, referred to, and fought for, so the label depends on the function a thing serves and the allegiance given to it, not on the thing itself. Second, the data does not settle whether 4:60 refers to a person, an institution, or a principle, so any specific modern identification goes beyond what the word alone establishes. Third, scholars differ on how broadly to apply the term to particular governments, rulers, or institutions today, and such judgments are best left to qualified scholarship and not made by applying a label to a person or group.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The lemma ذِكْر, a verbal noun of the root ذ ك ر, occurs **76 times in 36 surahs**: 63 times in Makki surahs and 13 in Madani surahs. The most frequent forms are the bare ذكر (×25), the definite الذكر (×14) and the indefinite accusative ذكرا (×10), followed by ذكرى (×5, "My remembrance/message"), للذكر (×4), بذكر (×3), ذكرنا (×2) and لذكر (×2). The remaining forms occur once each: كذكركم, والذكر, لذكرى, ذكركم, وذكر, وذكرا, بذكرهم, ذكرهم, ولذكر, بالذكر and ذكرك.

The word moves across a wide semantic range. At one end it is the human act of remembering or mentioning. At the other it is the revealed "Reminder" or "message" itself. The translation in the data reflects this range by rendering the same word as "remembrance," "reminder," "message," "mention," "report," "repute," "revelation" and even "the Qur'an." The groups below follow these senses. Some boundaries are uncertain, and those cases are noted.

### Remembrance of Allah as a devotional act
Here ذِكْر is the believer's act of remembering Allah, almost always in the construct ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ or with a divine pronoun. It is closely paired with prayer: "the remembrance of Allah and from prayer" (5:91), "establish prayer for My remembrance" (20:14), and "the remembrance of Allah and performance of prayer and giving of zakah" (24:37). It is set against distractions such as intoxicants and gambling, commerce, sale, wealth and children. It is also linked to the state of the heart, being assured, softened or humbly submissive.

>> أَلَا بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطۡمَئِنُّ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ

"Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured" (13:28).

In 2:200 and 33:41 the word appears as an intensified cognate object of the imperative ٱذۡكُرُواْ:

>> ٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ ذِكۡرٗا كَثِيرٗا

In 39:22 and 39:23 the remembrance of Allah stands next to "the best statement: a consistent Book." In these two verses the act of remembering and the revealed word may overlap, and the sense is not certain.

**References:** 2:200 (×2), 5:91, 13:28 (×2), 20:14, 20:42, 24:37, 29:45, 33:41, 38:32, 39:22, 39:23, 57:16, 58:19, 62:9, 63:9

### Turning away from, or heedlessness of, God's remembrance
In this group ذِكْر always has a divine possessor: ذِكْرِي, ذِكْرِنَا, ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِم or ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ. It is the object of verbs of aversion and neglect: turning away, turning one's back, being made heedless, having eyes covered, being blinded, or being made to forget. The subjects are those who reject, and the consequences named include "a depressed life," being gathered "blind," a devil appointed as companion, and "arduous punishment."

>> وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِكۡرِي

"And whoever turns away from My remembrance" (20:124).

It is uncertain whether these verses mean neglect of the act of remembering God or rejection of His revealed message. In 53:29 the data's translation chooses "Our message," while in 18:28 the same form is rendered "Our remembrance."

**References:** 18:28, 18:101, 20:124, 21:42, 23:110, 43:36, 53:29, 72:17

### The Reminder as revelation sent down or delivered
Here ذِكْر names the revealed message itself. It is the object or subject of verbs of descent and delivery: نزّل, أنزل, ألقي, آتى, and "comes to them." It is sent "from your Lord" or "from the Most Merciful," "through a man from among you," and it is "blessed" and "precise." The translation sometimes renders it simply as "the Qur'an" (15:9, 20:99, 65:10).

>> إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نَزَّلۡنَا ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ

"Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an and indeed, We will be its guardian" (15:9).

In 37:3 and 77:5 the indefinite ذِكۡرًا is the object of reciting and delivering, and the doers are those whom the translation identifies as reciters and "[angels]."

**References:** 3:58, 7:63, 7:69, 15:6, 15:9, 16:44, 20:99, 21:2, 21:50, 26:5, 37:3, 38:8 (×2), 54:25, 65:10, 77:5

### Reception and rejection of the message
These verses focus on how people respond to the Reminder once it has come. Some follow it (36:11). Many forget it, are led away from it, disbelieve in it, or turn from it. In 43:5 the possibility is raised of the message being turned away from a transgressing people.

>> بَلۡ أَتَيۡنَٰهُم بِذِكۡرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ عَن ذِكۡرِهِم مُّعۡرِضُونَ

"Rather, We have brought them their message, but they, from their message, are turning away" (23:71).

In 25:29 the translation renders الذكر as "the remembrance," but the phrase "after it had come to me" points toward the message sense.

**References:** 23:71 (×2), 25:18, 25:29, 36:11, 41:41, 43:5, 68:51

### The Qur'an characterised as "a reminder"
In these verses ذِكْر is a predicate describing the Qur'an. It usually appears in a restrictive construction (إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا / وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا) with the addressees "to the worlds." It is paired with "a clear Qur'an" (36:69) and contrasted with poetry. In 38:1 the Qur'an is said to be ذِي ٱلذِّكۡرِ, "containing reminder." In 43:44 the scope narrows to "for you and your people."

>> وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرٞ لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ

**References:** 12:104, 36:69, 38:1, 38:49, 38:87, 43:44, 68:52, 81:27

### Earlier revelation and its people
Here the Reminder is linked to revelation given before the Prophet. Examples include "the people of the message" whom the audience should ask, the reminder given to Moses and Aaron alongside "the criterion and a light," "the [previous] mention" before the Psalms, and the disbelievers' wish for "a message from [those of] the former peoples." In 21:24 the word appears twice, joining "the message for those with me and the message of those before me."

>> فَسۡـَٔلُوٓاْ أَهۡلَ ٱلذِّكۡرِ إِن كُنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ

**References:** 16:43, 21:7, 21:24 (×2), 21:48, 21:105, 37:168

### Remembrance as the aim and effect of the Qur'an
In these verses ذِكْر names the response the Qur'an is meant to produce in its hearers, not the revelation itself. Al-Qamar's refrain makes the Qur'an "easy for remembrance" and pairs the noun with the participle مُّدَّكِر. In 20:113 the diversified warnings may "cause them remembrance."

>> وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرٖ

"And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember."

**References:** 20:113, 54:17, 54:22, 54:32, 54:40

### Mention, report and repute
In a smaller set of verses the word carries its more general sense of speaking about or recalling someone or something:

- Joseph's request to be mentioned before the master, which Satan caused to be forgotten (12:42). Whether ربه here means "master" or "Lord" is not settled by the text; the translation chooses "master."
- The companion's promise to "make to you about it mention" (18:70).
- "A report" about Dhul-Qarnayn (18:83).
- "A mention of the mercy of your Lord" (19:2).
- "The mention of the Most Merciful" at which the disbelievers disbelieve (21:36).
- The Prophet's raised "repute" (94:4):

>> وَرَفَعۡنَا لَكَ ذِكۡرَكَ

In 21:10, "a Book in which is your mention," it is uncertain whether the word means a mention of the addressees, a reminder addressed to them, or their renown.

**References:** 12:42, 18:70, 18:83, 19:2, 21:10, 21:36, 94:4

## Patterns worth a researcher's attention

- **Makki and Madani distribution.** Of the 13 Madani occurrences, 11 belong to the devotional sense "remembrance of Allah." Only 3:58 and 65:10 refer to the revealed message. In the Makki material the message sense clearly dominates.
- **Two ways of naming the divine referent.** The explicit construct ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ appears 11 times, 8 of them in Madani surahs (5:91, 13:28 ×2, 24:37, 57:16, 58:19, 62:9, 63:9) and 3 in Makki surahs (29:45, 39:22, 39:23). The other Makki texts express the divine referent differently: through pronouns (ذِكۡرِي, ذِكۡرِنَا) or through رَبّ and ٱلرَّحۡمَٰن. They do so mostly in contexts of turning away.
- **The definite article.** The definite الذكر (×14), together with والذكر (3:58) and بالذكر (41:41), refers in every instance to revelation, either the message given to the Prophet or earlier revelation (16:43, 21:7, 21:105). The prefixed للذكر (54:17, 22, 32, 40) is the clear exception, where the noun names the act of remembering.
- **Cognate accusatives.** The indefinite ذِكۡرًا as an intensified object of the verb اذكروا (2:200, 33:41) occurs only in Madani surahs and only in the devotional sense.
- **Verbs of descent and delivery.** The Reminder is repeatedly the object of verbs of sending down (15:6, 15:9, 16:44, 21:50, 38:8, 54:25, 65:10). It is twice described as مُحۡدَث, "anew" (21:2, 26:5).
- **The charge of madness.** Twice the opponents' charge of madness follows directly on the Reminder: "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad" (15:6) and "when they hear the message, and they say, 'Indeed, he is mad'" (68:51). Twice the question "from among us?" is asked about it (38:8, 54:25).
- **Turning away.** Forms of أعرض cluster around the word (20:124, 21:42, 23:71, 72:17; compare 21:24, 26:5).
- **Satan's role.** Satan appears as the agent of forgetting or diversion in 12:42, 5:91, 58:19, 25:29 and 43:36.
- **Repeated formulas.** Two formulas recur almost verbatim: فَسۡـَٔلُوٓاْ أَهۡلَ ٱلذِّكۡرِ (16:43, 21:7) and إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرٞ لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ (38:87, 81:27; compare 12:104, 68:52).
- **Inconsistent translation.** The English rendering of the same Arabic varies considerably: "message," "reminder," "remembrance," "revelation," "the Qur'an." Comparison across verses should therefore rest on the Arabic and not on the translation.

## The use in 16:44

In 16:44 ٱلذِّكۡرَ is definite and is the object of أَنزَلۡنَآ, with the Prophet as recipient:

>> وَأَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلذِّكۡرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ

"And We revealed to you the message that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them and that they might give thought."

This places the verse squarely in the group of **the Reminder as revelation sent down**. It shares that group's typical features: the definite article, a verb of descent, and a Makki setting.

It also connects directly to the group on **earlier revelation**. The preceding verse, 16:43, uses أَهۡلَ ٱلذِّكۡرِ for those who possess prior revelation. Verse 16:44 itself opens with the earlier messengers' "clear proofs and written ordinances." The two adjacent occurrences thus set the dhikr given to the Prophet in continuity with what came before.

What distinguishes 16:44 within its group is the stated purpose clause. The Reminder is sent down so that the Prophet may "make clear" (لِتُبَيِّنَ) "what was sent down to them," leading to people who "might give thought." Here the dhikr is linked to an act of explanation by its recipient, which is not attested elsewhere in this data. The precise relation between ٱلذِّكۡرَ and مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ is not determined by the text alone. The word-by-word gloss ("the Remembrance") and the translation ("the message") differ in emphasis, which reflects the word's wider tension between remembrance and revealed message.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The lemma دِين occurs **92 times in 40 surahs**, 47 in Makki surahs and 45 in Madani surahs. The definite form الدين is by far the most frequent (×47). Pronominal suffixes account for much of the remainder: دينكم ×10, دينهم ×10, دينه ×2, دينى ×2. The bare construct or indefinite forms are دين ×7 and دينا ×4. Prefixed forms are ودين ×3, للدين ×3, بالدين ×3 and بدينكم ×1. Several verses contain the word more than once: 2:217, 5:3 (three times), 9:33, 30:30, 42:13, 48:28, 61:9, 98:5 and 109:6. The word spans two broad semantic fields: **recompense/judgment** and **religion/devotion**. Within the second field, the contexts of use separate fairly clearly into the groups below.

### Recompense and the Day of Judgment

Here the word denotes the reckoning and requital of deeds. It most often appears in the fixed construct يوم الدين, rendered throughout as "the Day of Recompense":
>> مَٰلِكِ يَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ
"Sovereign of the Day of Recompense" (1:4).

It is paired with verbs of denial (كذّب) and belief (صدّق), and with scenes of punishment and forgiveness. Iblis is cursed "until the Day of Recompense" (15:35, 38:78). Three occurrences use بالدين without يوم, always as the object of denial: "No! But you deny the Recompense" (82:9). In 24:25, the only Madani instance, the possessive دينهم is rendered "their deserved recompense", the one place where a suffixed form carries this sense.

- 1:4, 15:35, 24:25, 26:82, 37:20, 38:78, 51:6, 51:12, 56:56, 70:26, 74:46, 82:9, 82:15, 82:17, 82:18, 83:11, 95:7, 107:1

### Devotion as belonging to God

In these verses الدين is the subject of a statement that it belongs, or must come to belong, to God. The sense leans toward devotion, worship or obedience rather than a named religion. The translation itself varies: "worship" in 2:193 and 16:52, but "the religion" in 8:39 and "the pure religion" in 39:3. Two Madani verses frame this as the aim of fighting:
>> وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ كُلُّهُۥ لِلَّهِۚ

The two Makki verses state it as a standing fact, each with a qualifying word:
>> أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُۚ

- 2:193, 8:39, 16:52, 39:3

### Sincerity of devotion (مخلصين له الدين)

This is a near-formulaic construction in which الدين is the object of the participle of أخلص, rendered "sincere to Him in religion". It accompanies verbs of worship and invocation (اعبد, ادعوا):
>> فَٱعۡبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصٗا لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ

In three verses it depicts people in peril at sea who supplicate sincerely and then relapse into associating others once delivered (10:22, 29:65, 31:32). Variants are مخلصا له ديني (39:14) and أخلصوا دينهم لله (4:146).

- 4:146, 7:29, 10:22, 29:65, 31:32, 39:2, 39:11, 39:14, 40:14, 40:65, 98:5

### The correct religion (الدين القيم) and directing one's face to it

Here the word names the upright, normative way. It is qualified by قيّم or القيمة and often paired with حنيف and the way of Abraham. A recurring closing formula is:
>> ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ

"That is the correct religion" is applied to exclusive worship of God (12:40), to the fitrah (30:30), to the sacred months (9:36), and to sincere worship, prayer and zakah (98:5). All three للدين occurrences belong here, in the imperative "Direct your face toward the religion".

- 6:161, 9:36, 10:105, 12:40, 30:30 (twice), 30:43, 98:5

### The religion chosen, ordained and approved by God

In these verses دين is the way God chooses, ordains, perfects or approves. It is frequently identified with Islam or with submission:
>> إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمُ

It is linked to Abraham and his descendants (2:132, 4:125, 22:78) and to the prophets from Noah onward (42:13). The indefinite دينا functions as a specifying accusative, as in "have approved for you Islam as religion" (5:3) and "whoever desires other than Islam as religion" (3:85). The phrase دين الله appears in 3:83, 24:2 and 110:2.

- 2:132, 2:256, 3:19, 3:83, 3:85, 4:125, 5:3 (two of its three occurrences), 22:78, 24:2, 24:55, 42:13 (twice), 110:2

### The religion of truth (دين الحق) made manifest

This is a set formula in which the Messenger is sent "with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion":
>> هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ رَسُولَهُۥ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلۡحَقِّ لِيُظۡهِرَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِۦ

The second occurrence in each verse (الدين كله) refers to religion in a generic, plural sense, glossed "all religions". 9:29 uses the cognate verb with the noun: "who do not adopt the religion of truth".

- 9:29, 9:33 (twice), 48:28 (twice), 61:9 (twice)

### The believers' religion under hostility, defamation and apostasy

In these verses the believers' religion is something others seek to turn them from, defame, mock or despair of defeating. Leaving it is expressed with ارتدّ عن:
>> وَمَن يَرۡتَدِدۡ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ

Related collocations include طعن في الدين ("defaming the religion", 4:46; "defame your religion", 9:12) and "taken your religion in ridicule and amusement" (5:57). Opponents are identified by whether they "fight you because of religion" (60:8, 60:9). In 8:49 the hypocrites claim "Their religion has deluded those [Muslims]."

- 2:217 (twice), 4:46, 5:3 (one occurrence: "despaired of [defeating] your religion"), 5:54, 5:57, 8:49, 9:12, 60:8, 60:9

### Religion as the bond and practice of the community

Here الدين marks membership in and obligations of the believing community: "your brothers in religion" (9:11, 33:5), seeking help "for the religion" (8:72), and obtaining "understanding in the religion" (9:122). In 49:16 it refers to a professed faith that some would announce to God.

- 8:72, 9:11, 9:122, 33:5, 49:16

### The religion of others

The word also describes the religion of the People of the Scripture, polytheists, or Pharaoh's people, usually with the suffixes دينهم or دينكم. It is typically censured. Such religion is deluded by invention (3:24), carried to excess (لا تغلوا في دينكم, 4:171, 5:77), confused by "partners" (6:137), or ordained by them without God's consent (42:21). It is taken "as amusement and diversion" (6:70, 7:51), and its holders have "divided their religion and become sects":
>> إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمۡ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعٗا

In 40:26 Pharaoh fears Moses "will change your religion". In 3:73 the word occurs within reported speech urging trust only in those "who follow your religion".

- 3:24, 3:73, 4:171, 5:77, 6:70, 6:137, 6:159, 7:51, 30:32, 40:26, 42:21

### First-person declarations of one's religion

In these verses the Prophet sets his own religion against that of his hearers:
>> لَكُمۡ دِينُكُمۡ وَلِيَ دِينِ

"For you is your religion, and for me is my religion" (109:6). In 10:104 the address "if you are in doubt as to my religion" leads into a statement of whom he worships. Both occurrences of دينى and the ya-less دين in 109:6 fall here.

- 10:104, 109:6 (twice)

### Law or custom of a ruler

In the Joseph narrative the phrase دين الملك is glossed "the law", though the translation keeps "religion":
>> مَا كَانَ لِيَأۡخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ

The context of detaining a brother suggests a legal or customary sense. Because the translation and gloss diverge, the precise nuance should be treated as uncertain.

- 12:76

## Patterns worth a researcher's attention

- **The recompense sense is overwhelmingly Makki.** 17 of the 18 occurrences are in Makki surahs; 24:25 is the only Madani one. يوم الدين is exclusively Makki, and all three instances of بالدين are Makki objects of "deny".
- **Confrontational and communal uses are Madani.** Fighting, apostasy, defamation, "brothers in religion" and the formula دين الحق ... على الدين كله occur only in Madani surahs. دينكم is mainly Madani (8 of 10), whereas دينهم is evenly split (5 Makki, 5 Madani).
- **The sincerity formula is largely Makki.** مخلصين/مخلصا له الدين accounts for 9 of its 11 occurrences in Makki surahs, clustered in surahs 39 and 40. It recurs in a set sea-peril narrative (10:22, 29:65, 31:32).
- **The verb أقم has two objects.** أقم وجهك للدين is restricted to Makki surahs (10:105, 30:30, 30:43). أقيموا الدين appears in 42:13.
- **Qualifiers cluster around a small set.** These are القيم/قيما/القيمة, الخالص, الحق, and واصبا (16:52 only). حنيف/حنفاء co-occurs in 4:125, 6:161, 10:105, 30:30 and 98:5, often with the way of Abraham.
- **Recurring collocations.** Taking religion as play or ridicule appears in 5:57, 6:70 and 7:51, with هزو/لعب/لهو in varying order. "Divided their religion and become sects" is shared by 6:159 and 30:32, with the opposing injunction in 42:13. "Do not commit excess in your religion" appears in 4:171 and 5:77, and "revert from his religion" in 2:217 and 5:54.
- **Senses overlap within single verses.** 30:30 and 98:5 combine the sincerity and "correct religion" uses. 5:3 shifts within one verse from the believers' religion under threat to religion perfected and approved. The translation also renders الدين as "worship" in 2:193 and 16:52, but as "the religion" in the parallel 8:39.

## The use in 16:52

>> وَلَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِبًاۚ أَفَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ تَتَّقُونَ

"And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is [due] worship constantly. Then is it other than Allah that you fear"

The occurrence belongs with **devotion as belonging to God**. Its structure (fronted له + الدين + a qualifier) closely matches 39:3, أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُۚ. The difference is that واصبا adds a temporal dimension ("constantly") where الخالص adds purity. The verse sets this devotion beside God's ownership of all in the heavens and the earth, as 3:83 links God's religion to the submission of "those within the heavens and earth". It then closes with a question about fear (تتقون), which suggests obedience and reverence owed rather than a named religion.

The data's translation and gloss both render الدين here as "worship", as in 2:193. The parallel 8:39, however, is translated "the religion, all of it". The boundary between "worship/obedience" and "religion" in this construction is therefore not sharply drawn in the material itself. Unlike the Madani 2:193 and 8:39, which frame this belonging as an outcome to be achieved, 16:52 states it, as 39:3 does, as an existing and permanent fact in a Makki context.

## The Lemma عِبْرَة in 16:66: Usage and Differentiation

### 1. The occurrence under study

>> وَإِنَّ لَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ لَعِبۡرَةٗۖ نُّسۡقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِۦ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ فَرۡثٖ وَدَمٖ لَّبَنًا خَالِصٗا سَآئِغٗا لِّلشَّـٰرِبِينَ

Translation: "And indeed, for you in grazing livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excretion and blood - pure milk, palatable to drinkers" (16:66, Makki).

- **Form:** لَعِبْرَةً is the indefinite noun عِبْرَة, preceded by the emphatic *lām*. It is the predicate of إِنَّ. The gloss given is "(is) a lesson."
- **Construction:** The phrase follows the pattern إِنَّ + لَكُمۡ + فِي + [object of reflection] + لَعِبۡرَةٗ. The lesson is located *in* something concrete, here ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰم.
- **Content of the lesson:** Unlike most other occurrences, 16:66 does not point back to a preceding matter with ذَٰلِكَ. It states the lesson immediately afterwards: pure, palatable milk produced "between excretion and blood." The عِبْرَة is the striking contrast between the impure surroundings and the pure product.
- **Addressees:** The lesson is "for you" (لَكُمۡ), addressed generally. No qualified group such as "those of vision" is named.

### 2. The full distribution of عِبْرَة (6 occurrences)

| Ref. | Period | Object of the lesson | Recipients |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3:13 | Madani | Two armies that met (ذَٰلِكَ) | لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ, "those of vision" |
| 12:111 | Makki | "their stories" (قَصَصِهِمۡ) | لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ, "those of understanding" |
| 16:66 | Makki | Livestock (ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰم) | لَكُمۡ, "for you" |
| 23:21 | Makki | Livestock (ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰم) | لَكُمۡ, "for you" |
| 24:44 | Madani | Alternation of night and day (ذَٰلِكَ) | لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ, "those who have vision" |
| 79:26 | Makki | (ذَٰلِكَ) | لِّمَن يَخۡشَىٰٓ, "whoever would fear [Allah]" |

**Observations:**
- **Always indefinite.** In all six places the word is indefinite (عِبۡرَةٗ). Five of the six carry the emphatic *lām* after إِنَّ. The exception is 12:111, which uses لَقَدۡ كَانَ instead.
- **Three spheres of reflection:**
  - **History and events:** the battle in 3:13 and the stories in 12:111.
  - **Created nature:** livestock in 16:66 and 23:21, and night and day in 24:44.
  - **A referent outside the data:** the ذَٰلِكَ in 79:26. The data does not include its context, so the object of that lesson cannot be identified from the texts given.
- **The recipients are usually qualified.** In 3:13, 12:111, 24:44 and 79:26, the benefit is limited to those with perception (ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰر), intellect (ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰب), or fear (يَخۡشَىٰٓ). The two livestock passages (16:66, 23:21) instead address everyone with لَكُمۡ. This suggests the lesson drawn from livestock is presented as accessible to all, through common daily experience.
- **Period:** Both Madani occurrences (3:13, 24:44) share the closing لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ.

### 3. 16:66 compared with its parallel, 23:21

>> وَإِنَّ لَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ لَعِبۡرَةٗۖ نُّسۡقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ كَثِيرَةٞ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ

Translation: "And indeed, for you in livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from that which is in their bellies, and for you in them are numerous benefits, and from them you eat" (23:21).

- **Opening:** The two verses open identically, up to and including نُّسۡقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِي.
- **Pronoun:** 16:66 has بُطُونِهِۦ (masculine singular pronoun), while 23:21 has بُطُونِهَا (feminine pronoun).
- **Emphasis of 16:66:** It narrows the lesson to one marvel, the purity of the milk, shown through the contrast فَرۡثٖ وَدَمٖ / لَبَنًا خَالِصٗا.
- **Emphasis of 23:21:** It widens the lesson to the general utility of livestock: drink, "numerous benefits," and food.
- **Translation note:** The translation renders the same word ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰم as "grazing livestock" in 16:66 and "livestock" in 23:21. This is a difference in the English only.

### 4. Differentiation from similar Qur'anic terms

#### عِبْرَة and آيَة

The only closely related term in the data is آيَة, which appears beside عِبْرَة in 3:13:

>> قَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ ءَايَةٞ فِي فِئَتَيۡنِ ٱلۡتَقَتَاۖ ... إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبۡرَةٗ لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ

Translation: "Already there has been for you a sign in the two armies which met ... Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision."

Within this one verse the two words are distinguished by position and audience:

- **آيَة ("a sign")** opens the verse. It is the event itself, presented to "you" in general.
- **عِبْرَة ("a lesson")** closes the verse. It refers back to that event with ذَٰلِكَ and is restricted to "those of vision."

So the data presents آيَة as the phenomenon displayed, and عِبْرَة as what a perceptive observer takes from it.

#### Related terms in 12:111

12:111 places عِبْرَة beside several other terms:
- تَصۡدِيق, "confirmation"
- تَفۡصِيل, "detailed explanation"
- هُدٗى, "guidance"
- رَحۡمَة, "mercy"

These describe the nature of the revelation. عِبۡرَة, by contrast, is located in the stories (قَصَصِهِمۡ) and is directed at "those of understanding." Guidance and mercy are directed at "a people who believe."

#### The translation of 79:26

The given translation renders لَعِبۡرَةٗ there as "a warning," whereas the other five verses use "a lesson." This reflects the translator's choice and the verse's audience, "whoever would fear [Allah]." It does not indicate a different Arabic word.

#### Limits of the data

Other Qur'anic terms that might be compared with عِبْرَة are not represented in the data supplied. A textual differentiation from them therefore cannot be made here. That would require their occurrences to be provided.

### 5. Summary for 16:66

In 16:66, عِبْرَة denotes an emphatic, indefinite "lesson" found in a familiar created thing, livestock. It is addressed to all hearers without restriction. Its content is spelled out at once: pure milk drawn from between excretion and blood.

Its closest parallel, 23:21, shares the frame but broadens the lesson to the general benefits of livestock. Its closest related term in the data, آيَة (3:13), names the observable sign, while عِبْرَة names the lesson drawn from it.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The sequence ما + مَلَكَتْ + يَمِين occurs **14 times in 7 surahs** (4, 16, 23, 24, 30, 33, 70). Four occurrences are in Makki surahs and ten in Madani surahs, and Surah 4 and Surah 33 together account for eight. The verb is always the feminine perfect مَلَكَتْ, agreeing with يَمِين. The noun is usually the plural أَيْمَٰن with a pronoun suffix: -كُم ×6 (including وَمَا at 4:36 and مِمَّا at 24:33), -هُم ×4 (including وَمَا at 33:50), and -هُنَّ ×2. The singular يَمِينُكَ occurs twice (4:3 and 4:24 aside, see below). The relative ما is used of persons, so the data's translations render it as "those whom", while the glosses vary between "what" and "whom".

### Marriage options and prohibitions

In these Madani legal passages the phrase names a category of women that is distinct from free women. It is offered as an alternative when a man fears injustice among several wives (4:3) or cannot afford to marry "free, believing women" (4:25). In 4:24 it is set apart by an exception (إِلَّا) from the prohibition on married women. Here it is contrasted with ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰت and with marriage to free women. 4:25 specifies them as "believing slave girls" and requires the "permission of their people" and "due compensation".

>> فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْ فَوَٰحِدَةً أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۚ

"But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one or those your right hand possesses."

- 4:3, 4:24, 4:25

### Lawful intimacy alongside wives

Here the phrase is paired directly with أَزۡوَٰج, usually through أَوۡ or the conjunction وَ, as the two lawful categories of intimacy. In 23:6 and 70:30 it appears in an identical formula exempting the believers from blame. In Surah 33 the same pairing is applied to the Prophet, with the singular يَمِينُكَ: once among what is made lawful to him (33:50), and once as the sole exception after further marriages are closed to him (33:52). In 33:50 the phrase is also applied to the believers in general, with أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ.

>> إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ غَيۡرُ مَلُومِينَ

"Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed" (23:6)

>> إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ يَمِينُكَۗ

"except what your right hand possesses" (33:52)

- 23:6, 70:30, 33:50, 33:50, 33:52

### Members of a woman's household before whom she may appear

In these two passages the possessors are women (أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ). The phrase stands in a list of close persons, chiefly kin, before whom women may show adornment (24:31) or toward whom there is "no blame upon women" (33:55). It follows نِسَآئِهِنَّ in both lists. The texts do not specify the sex of those so possessed, so the precise scope of the category here is uncertain from the data alone.

>> وَلَا نِسَآئِهِنَّ وَلَا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّۗ

"or their women or those their right hands possess." (33:55)

- 24:31, 33:55

### Objects of ethical obligation

Here the phrase designates people toward whom the owners have duties. In 4:36 they close a list of those owed good treatment (إِحۡسَٰن), after parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, neighbours, companions and the traveller. In 24:33 those "who seek a contract [for eventual emancipation]" are drawn from among them (مِمَّا), and the owners are told to contract with them and to "give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you".

>> وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ

- 4:36, 24:33

### Parable of unequal provision

In two Makki passages the phrase is used rhetorically, not legally. The relation between owners and those they possess serves as an analogy. Both passages concern رِزۡق, both use the predicate سَوَآء ("equal"), and both turn on the owners' unwillingness to treat their possessed as equals in what they have been provided.

>> هَل لَّكُم مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُم مِّن شُرَكَآءَ فِي مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ فَأَنتُمۡ فِيهِ سَوَآءٞ

"Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you so that you are equal therein"

- 16:71, 30:28

## Patterns worth attention

- **Makki versus Madani:** The Makki occurrences fall into two fixed types: the parable of provision (16:71, 30:28) and the formula on wives (23:6, 70:30). All regulatory and household uses (Surahs 4, 24, 33) are Madani.
- **The fixed formula:** 23:6 and 70:30 are identical in Arabic. The data's translations differ only slightly: "they will not be blamed" and "they are not to be blamed".
- **Pronoun distribution:** The feminine أَيْمَٰنُهُنَّ occurs only in the two lists about women's adornment and presence (24:31, 33:55). The singular يَمِينُكَ occurs only in Surah 33, addressed to the Prophet. The second-person -كُم dominates the Madani legal and ethical passages, and also appears in the Makki parable at 30:28.
- **Recurring collocations:** The phrase is joined to أَزۡوَٰج in five places (23:6, 70:30, 33:50 twice, and implicitly 4:3 through وَٰحِدَة). It follows إِلَّا in exceptive constructions (4:24, 33:52, and the إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ of 23:6 and 70:30). It is often linked by أَوۡ as one alternative among others (4:3, 23:6, 70:30, 24:31).
- **Prepositional framing:** مِن with the phrase marks a subset drawn from the possessed in 4:25 (فَمِن مَّا), 24:33 (مِمَّا) and 30:28 (مِّن مَّا). In 16:71 it is governed by عَلَىٰ, as the recipients of what is "handed over".
- **فَتَيَات:** The phrase is associated with فَتَيَٰت ("slave girls") in 4:25 and 24:33.

## The use in 16:71

16:71 belongs clearly to the parable group, alongside 30:28.

>> فَمَا ٱلَّذِينَ فُضِّلُواْ بِرَآدِّي رِزۡقِهِمۡ عَلَىٰ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌۚ

"But those who were favored would not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess so they would be equal to them therein."

The two verses share the vocabulary of رِزۡق and the predicate فِيهِ سَوَآء. 16:71 differs from 30:28 in three ways:

- It is framed in the third person (أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ) rather than as a direct second-person question.
- It opens with a statement that "Allah has favored some of you over others in provision".
- It closes with a rebuke: "Then is it the favor of Allah they reject".

Its form ما ملكت أيمانهم is shared with the Makki formula in 23:6 and 70:30, yet its function is entirely different. There the phrase names a lawful category paired with wives. Here the owners' reluctance to equalise with those they possess becomes the basis of an argument, so the same morphological form serves two distinct Makki purposes.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The lemma **كاذِب** (root ك ذ ب, active participle) occurs 32 times across 21 surahs: 22 in Makki surahs and 10 in Madani surahs. The masculine plural dominates. The oblique form الكذبين appears ×10, the emphatic predicate لكذبون ×9, indefinite كذبين ×3, definite nominative الكذبون ×3 and indefinite كذبون ×1. The singular appears as كذب ×2 and كذبا ×2, and the feminine as كاذبة ×1 and كذبة ×1. In almost every case the word is predicative or classificatory: it assigns a person or group to the category "liars" rather than describing a single act of speech.

### Accusation levelled against messengers

In these passages opponents apply the word to a messenger, almost always governed by a verb of supposition (ظنّ). The charge is put as conjecture ("we think"), and it is regularly joined to dismissive remarks: "foolishness" in 7:66, and "a man like ourselves" in 11:27 and 26:186. The speakers are the disbelieving "eminent ones" of a people, or Pharaoh. In 40:28 a believer from Pharaoh's family turns the charge into a conditional set against صادقا:
>> وَإِن يَكُ كَٰذِبٗا فَعَلَيۡهِ كَذِبُهُۥۖ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقٗا
"And if he should be lying, then upon him is [the consequence of] his lie; but if he should be truthful."

- 7:66, 11:27, 26:186, 28:38, 40:28, 40:37

### Distinguishing the truthful from the liars

Here the word marks one side of an open question that testing, evidence or outcome will settle. It is paired explicitly with the verb صدق in 9:43, 12:26, 27:27 and 29:3:
>> فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
"and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars."

The agent of discovery varies. It is Allah (29:3), the Prophet (9:43), Solomon (27:27) and a witness's test of the torn shirt (12:26). In 11:93 it is the coming outcome itself: "You are going to know ... who is a liar." In 12:74 the word appears in a hypothetical posed by accusers: "if you should be liars."

- 9:43, 11:93, 12:26, 12:74, 27:27, 29:3

### Oath, curse and legal testimony

In these occurrences the word belongs to a formal procedure in which the curse of Allah or the standing of testimony depends on who is "of the liars." 3:61 invokes "the curse of Allah upon the liars [among us]." 24:7 and 24:8 set out the oath formulae of mutual testimony. 24:13 makes the absence of four witnesses the criterion by which slanderers are judged liars "in the sight of Allah."

- 3:61, 24:7, 24:8, 24:13

### Divine testimony against the hypocrites

In this group Allah's knowledge or testimony is set directly against the oaths or professions of the hypocrites. The verb يحلف appears in 9:42, 9:107 and 58:18. The frame والله يشهد / والله يعلم followed by إنّ … لكاذبون recurs:
>> وَٱللَّهُ يَشۡهَدُ إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
"and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars."

63:1 is notable because the hypocrites' stated words, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah," are affirmed as true in content, yet the speakers are still declared liars. The text thus shows the label applying to the speakers rather than to the proposition they utter.

- 9:42, 9:107, 58:18, 59:11, 63:1

### Verdict on the claims of disbelievers and associators

Here the word closes a report of a false claim or a false hope with a verdict on those who hold it. The claims include that "Allah has begotten" (37:152), the promise to carry others' sins (29:12), and the justification of intercessors (39:3). The word is set against "the truth" brought by Allah (23:90), and it is joined to كفار in 39:3. In 16:39 the disbelievers will "know that they were liars." In 16:86 the verdict is spoken by the "partners" themselves to those who invoked them. The referent of 26:223, "most of them are liars," is not identified within the ayah given, so its placement here is provisional.

- 6:28, 16:39, 16:86, 16:105, 23:90, 26:223, 29:12, 37:152, 39:3

### Feminine form as attribute or noun

The two feminine occurrences fall outside the human "liar" category. In 96:16 كَٰذِبَةٍ qualifies a "forelock" and is paired with خَاطِئَةٖ ("A lying, sinning forelock"). In 56:2 the data glosses كَاذِبَةٌ as "a denial" ("There is, at its occurrence, no denial"). That gloss treats the form as a substantive rather than an adjective, and its exact sense is less certain than in the other groups.

- 56:2, 96:16

## Patterns worth attention

- **Makki–Madani distribution.** All accusations against messengers and all feminine forms are Makki. Every Madani occurrence falls under oath and testimony (3:61, 24:7, 24:8, 24:13) or under the hypocrites and their oaths (9:42, 9:43, 9:107, 58:18, 59:11, 63:1).
- **Emphatic لكاذبون.** All nine occurrences of لكذبون follow إنّ (إنهم / إنكم / إن المنافقين) and function as a definitive verdict. In eight of them the verdict comes from the narrative or divine voice. In 16:86 it is spoken by the "partners" within a scene.
- **Restrictive هم الكاذبون.** The three occurrences of الكذبون all carry a separating pronoun that confines the description to a specific group: 16:105 (أولئك هم), 24:13 (فأولئك عند الله هم) and 58:18 (ألا إنهم هم).
- **من الكاذبين with ظنّ.** The partitive "of the liars" is the characteristic form of accusation, whether introduced by نظنك or لأظنه (7:66, 26:186, 28:38) or posed as a question (27:27). The indefinite accusative appears in parallel constructions (11:27, 40:37).
- **Pairing with truthfulness.** Contrast with صدق or صادق recurs in 9:43, 12:26, 27:27, 29:3 and 40:28. Pairing with other negative attributes appears in 39:3 (كفار) and 96:16 (خاطئة). In 40:28 the same ayah also contains the intensive كذّاب, which belongs to a different lemma.

## The use in 16:105

In 16:105 the word belongs to the group of verdicts on the claims of disbelievers. It shares the restrictive construction found only in 24:13 and 58:18:
>> وَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
"and it is those who are the liars"

It is distinctive in two ways. First, the participle is preceded in the same ayah by a related form from the same root, يَفۡتَرِي ٱلۡكَذِبَ ("invent falsehood"). Second, the restriction operates at two levels: إنما limits the inventing of falsehood to "those who do not believe in the verses of Allah," and أولئك هم then limits the title "the liars" to them. In context this reverses the accusation that, in the first group, opponents direct at messengers. Like 39:3, the ayah ties lying to disbelief, here specifically disbelief in the verses of Allah.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The lemma طَبَعَ occurs **11 times in 9 surahs**: 6 times in Makki surahs (7:100, 7:101, 10:74, 16:108, 30:59, 40:35) and 5 times in Madani surahs (4:155, 9:87, 9:93, 47:16, 63:3). The written forms are طبع ×3, يطبع ×3, وطبع ×2, ونطبع ×1, نطبع ×1 and فطبع ×1. These counts group spellings by consonantal shape, so the form وطبع covers both the passive وَطُبِعَ (9:87) and the active وَطَبَعَ (9:93). In every occurrence the verb takes the preposition عَلَىٰ, and its object is the heart (قُلُوب or قَلۡب). The data therefore shows a single, consistently figurative sense: God's sealing of the heart against understanding or belief. The groups below separate the contexts in which this one sense is used, not distinct meanings.

### Sealing as a recurring divine pattern (the كَذَٰلِكَ formula)

Here the sealing is presented as a general law. It is introduced by كَذَٰلِكَ ("thus") and expressed with the imperfect, often after an account of earlier peoples who rejected their messengers. The sealed are named by a category: the disbelievers, the transgressors, those who do not know, or the arrogant tyrant. In 7:101 and 10:74 the formula closes a near-identical narrative frame:
>> فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَطۡبَعُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
>> فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ بِهِۦ مِن قَبۡلُۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَطۡبَعُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
In 40:35 the formula follows a description of "Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without an authority having come to them". It ends: "Thus does Allah seal over every heart [belonging to] an arrogant tyrant".
- 7:101, 10:74, 30:59, 40:35

### Sealing as the consequence of sin and rejection

In these ayat the sealing is tied to an explicit cause, and a consequence clause follows it. In 4:155 the cause is stated with بِ: "Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few".
>> بَلۡ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهَا بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗا
Here the sealing is set against the speakers' own claim, "Our hearts are wrapped". In 7:100 it is paired with God's power to "afflict them for their sins", and the result is that "they do not hear".
- 4:155, 7:100

### Sealing of those who stay behind or revert

These Madani ayat describe people defined by their conduct toward the Prophet's community. Some were "satisfied to be with those who stay behind" (9:87, 9:93). Others "believed, and then they disbelieved" (63:3). Each ends with a clause negating comprehension: فَهُمۡ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ ("so they do not understand") in 9:87 and 63:3, and فَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ("so they do not know") in 9:93. Two of the three use the passive voice:
>> فَطُبِعَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ
- 9:87, 9:93, 63:3

### Identifying a class: أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ

In these two ayat the sealing serves as a defining description. A demonstrative and a relative clause mark out a group of people. The verb is in the perfect, with God as the named subject, and a second clause adds a further characterization. In 47:16 the sealed are those who listen to the Prophet and then ask, "What has he said just now?" They are further described as those "who have followed their [own] desires". In 16:108 the sealed are further described as "the heedless".
>> أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡ
- 16:108, 47:16

## Patterns worth a researcher's attention

- **Tense and surah type:** Five of the six Makki occurrences are imperfect (7:100, 7:101, 10:74, 30:59, 40:35). All five Madani occurrences are perfect. 16:108 is the only Makki perfect.
- **Voice and agent:** The passive (طُبِعَ) appears only in Madani ayat (9:87, 63:3). The first-person plural (نَطۡبَعُ) appears only in Makki ayat (7:100, 10:74). Elsewhere God is the named subject (4:155, 7:101, 9:93, 16:108, 30:59, 40:35, 47:16).
- **Fixed collocation:** Every occurrence has the pattern طَبَعَ عَلَىٰ + heart. In 4:155 the heart is referred to by the pronoun عَلَيۡهَا. 16:108 alone extends the object beyond the heart, to hearing and vision.
- **Consequence clauses with فَ:** Several ayat follow the sealing with a negated faculty or response. These are لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ (7:100), لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ (9:87, 63:3), لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ (9:93) and لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ (4:155). In 30:59 the related idea instead describes the recipients: "those who do not know".
- **Parallel pairs:** 7:101 and 10:74 share nearly identical wording and differ in the agent (ٱللَّهُ / first-person plural) and the object (ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ / ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ). Likewise, 9:87 and 9:93 differ in voice (passive / active) and in the final verb (يَفۡقَهُونَ / يَعۡلَمُونَ).
- **Stated causes:** A cause is made explicit in 4:155 (بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ), 7:100 (بِذُنُوبِهِمۡ) and 63:3 (believing, then disbelieving). In the remaining ayat the cause is either implied by the narrative or not stated within the ayah itself.

## The use in 16:108

In 16:108 the verb طَبَعَ is a perfect with God as the named subject, set inside the identifying construction أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ … This places it squarely with 47:16, whose opening words it shares exactly:
>> أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَسَمۡعِهِمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰفِلُونَ
"Those are the ones over whose hearts and hearing and vision Allah has sealed, and it is those who are the heedless".

Within the data, 16:108 is distinctive in three ways:

- It is the only Makki occurrence in the perfect.
- It is the only one in which the seal covers hearing and vision as well as hearts.
- Its closing characterization is a nominal sentence of identity (هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰفِلُونَ, "it is those who are the heedless"), not the negated-verb consequence clause (فَهُمۡ لَا …) found in 4:155, 7:100, 9:87, 9:93 and 63:3.

Heedlessness nonetheless stands in the same semantic field as the incapacities named in those clauses (not hearing, not understanding, not knowing). The ayah itself does not state a cause for the sealing. Whether it belongs with the cause-and-consequence ayat would depend on the surrounding verses, which are not included in this data, so that question is left open here.

## Usage across the Qur'an

The root ج ه ل occurs **24 times in 17 surahs**: 15 occurrences in Makki surahs and 9 in Madani surahs. It appears in nine forms:

- **ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ** (6)
- **ٱلْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ** (4)
- **بِجَهَٰلَةٍ** (4)
- **تَجْهَلُونَ** (4)
- **ٱلْجَٰهِلُونَ** (2)
- **ٱلْجَاهِلُ** (1)
- **يَجْهَلُونَ** (1)
- **جَٰهِلُونَ** (1)
- **جَهُولًا** (1)

Most of these are nominal: active participles in the singular and plural, the abstract noun **ٱلْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ**, the noun **جَهَٰلَة**, and the intensive adjective **جَهُول**. The verbal forms that occur are all imperfect (**تَجْهَلُونَ**, **يَجْهَلُونَ**). No perfect-tense verb from this root appears in the data.

### Wrongdoing committed in a state of ignorance

In this group the root describes the condition in which a harmful act is done, not a person's fixed identity. Three of the four **بِجَهَٰلَةٍ** occurrences attach it to "doing wrong" (**عمل السوء**), and each time it is followed by repentance and divine forgiveness. 4:17 describes those who "do wrong in ignorance [or carelessness] and then repent soon after." The bracketed "[or carelessness]" in that translation shows that the exact sense is open: the phrase could mean not knowing, or acting heedlessly. 49:6 uses the same phrase for harming a people on the basis of an unverified report, which ends not in repentance but in being "regretful." 12:89 uses **جَٰهِلُونَ** for Joseph's brothers, set against **عَلِمۡتُم** ("Do you know"). Their deed was deliberate, which suggests the root can cover moral folly as well as missing information.

- 4:17, 6:54, 16:119, 49:6, 12:89

### "Being among the ignorant": a state warned against or sought refuge from

Here the plural participle always appears in the construction **كون + مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ**. It is spoken by or to a prophet: Moses (2:67), Muhammad (6:35), Noah (11:46) and Joseph (12:33). Being "among the ignorant" is a category that even the righteous must guard against. In 11:46 it is tied directly to asking "for that about which you have no knowledge." In 12:33 it is tied to inclining toward a seductive invitation, so the sense extends from lack of knowledge to yielding to impulse. In 2:67 it answers a charge of mockery, where it seems to mean frivolous or unbecoming conduct.

>> أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ

- 2:67, 6:35, 11:46, 12:33

### Prophets' verdict on their peoples: "a people behaving ignorantly"

The phrase **قَوۡمٞ تَجۡهَلُونَ** / **قَوۡمٗا تَجۡهَلُونَ** is a prophet's judgement on his community.
